title.zh: 卷一百三十 志第八十三 樂五
title.raw: 卷一百三十 志第八十三 樂五 Volume 130 Treatises 83: Music 5

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，經營多難，其於稽古飾治之事，時靡遑暇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong crossed south, amid managing many hardships, as to matters of examining antiquity and adorning governance, he at times had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong fled south, the court faced one crisis after another, and he rarely had time for the scholarly ritual work of looking to antiquity and polishing statecraft.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，首詔有司曰：“朕承祖宗遺澤，獲托臣民之上，扶顛持危，夙夜痛悼。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan, he first issued an edict to the relevant offices, saying: "I inherit the blessed legacy of the ancestors and have been placed above the officials and the people; righting what is overturned and holding up what is endangered, I grieve day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyan (1127), he issued his first edict to the ministries: "I have inherited our ancestors' grace and been set above the people; as I struggle to right the realm, I grieve night and day.

sentences.zh: 況於聞樂以自為樂，實增感於朕心。

translations.literal: How much more, to hear music and take it for one's own pleasure—this truly adds to the distress in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: To hear music and take pleasure in it would only deepen my anguish.

sentences.zh: ”二年，復下詔曰：“朕方日極憂念，屏遠聲樂，不令過耳。

translations.literal: " In the second year, he again issued an edict, saying: "I am daily consumed with anxious thoughts; I keep music at a distance and do not allow it to reach my ears.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year he decreed again: "I am steeped in worry every day; I banish all music and will not let a note reach my ears.

sentences.zh: 承平典故，雖實廢名存，亦所不忍，悉從減罷。

translations.literal: The precedents of peaceful times, though in practice abolished, still remained in name, and he could not bear this either; all were accordingly reduced and suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Even ceremonial relics of calmer days, though hollow in practice, were more than he could stomach to keep on the books—and he ordered them all cut back or discontinued.

sentences.zh: ”是歲，始據光武舊禮，以建武二載創立郊祀，乃十一月壬寅祀天配祖，敕東京起奉大樂登歌法物等赴行在所，就維揚江都築壇行事。

translations.literal: " That year, beginning to follow Emperor Guangwu's old rites, with the suburban sacrifice established in the second year of Jianwu, on the day ren-yin of the eleventh month they sacrificed to Heaven with the ancestors as associates; an edict ordered the Eastern Capital to send the great ritual music, sacrificial ascent music, ritual implements, and the like to the traveling palace, and a sacrificial altar was built at Jiangdu on the Yangzi to conduct the rites.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court, following Guangwu's precedent from the second year of Jianwu, revived the suburban sacrifice. On ren-yin day of the eleventh month they offered to Heaven with imperial ancestors in attendance. Orders went out to move the great liturgical music, ascent hymns, and ritual paraphernalia from the eastern capital to the temporary seat of government, and an altar was erected at Jiangdu on the Yangtze to perform the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 凡鹵簿、樂舞之類，率多未備，嚴更警場，至就取中軍金鼓，權一時之用。

translations.literal: As for processional guards, music and dance, and the like, most were not yet prepared; for the strict changing of watches and the warning ground, they even took the central army's gongs and drums for provisional use.
translations.idiomatic: Processional arrays, dances, and supporting ensembles were still largely missing; for the solemn watch changes at the ritual ground the court even borrowed the central army's bronze drums and gongs as a stopgap.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，始饗明堂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, they first offered at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 the court held its first Bright Hall sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 時初駐會稽，而渡江舊樂復皆毀散。

translations.literal: At that time the court had only recently taken up residence at Kuaiji, and the old music brought across the river had again all been destroyed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The court had only recently settled at Kuaiji, and the ritual music brought south had again been lost in the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蘇遲等言：“國朝大禮作樂，依儀合於壇殿上設登歌，壇殿下設宮架。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Su Chi and others said: "For great state ceremonies of our dynasty, music is performed according to the rites: ascent music should be set up on the altar platform and in the hall above, and the palace frame below the altar platform and hall.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Sacrifices Su Chi and others reported: "For our dynasty's greatest ceremonies, ritual prescribes ascent music on the altar and in the upper hall, with the palace frame ensemble below the altar and hall.

sentences.zh: 今親祠登歌樂器尚闕，宣和添用籥色，未及頒降，州郡無從可以創製，宜權用望祭禮例，止設登歌，用樂工四十有七人。

translations.literal: Now for the imperial sacrifice in person the ascent-music instruments are still lacking; the additional pipe colors added in the Xuanhe period have not yet been promulgated and distributed, and the prefectures and circuits have no basis on which to create them. It is appropriate provisionally to use the precedent of the suburban prospect sacrifice, setting up only ascent music, with forty-seven musicians.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent-music instruments for an imperial sacrifice in person are still missing; the extra pipe sections added in the Xuanhe era have not been issued, so the provinces cannot fabricate them. For now we should follow the suburban prospect-sacrifice precedent and use ascent music only, with forty-seven musicians.

sentences.zh: ”乃訪舊工，以備其數。

translations.literal: " They then sought out former craftsmen to make up the number.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then searched out veteran musicians to fill the roster.

sentences.zh: 四年，再饗，國子丞王普言：“按《書·舜典》，命夔曰：‘詩言誌，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when they again offered at the Bright Hall, National University Assistant Wang Pu said: "According to the 'Canon of Shun' in the Documents, [Shun] charged Kui, saying: 'Poetry expresses the intent; song prolongs the words; sound follows the prolongation; pitch harmonizes the sound.'
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, at the second Bright Hall sacrifice, National University Assistant Wang Pu argued: "The Canon of Shun in the Documents records Shun's charge to Kui: 'Poetry voices the mind; song extends the words; tone follows the extension; pitch harmonizes the tone.'

sentences.zh: ’蓋古者既作詩，從而歌之，然後以聲律協和而成曲。

translations.literal: ' In antiquity, once poetry was composed, they then sang it, and only afterward used pitch and tone to harmonize it into a complete melody.
translations.idiomatic: ' In antiquity one first composed the poem, then sang it, and only then set pitch and tone to shape a finished piece.

sentences.zh: 自曆代至於本朝，雅樂皆先製樂章而後成譜。

translations.literal: From successive dynasties down to our dynasty, for elegant music they always first composed the hymn text and only afterward completed the score.
translations.idiomatic: From earlier dynasties through our own, court music always began with the hymn text and only then received its score.

sentences.zh: 祟寧以後，乃先製譜，後命詞，於是詞律不相諧協，且與俗樂無異。

translations.literal: After Chongning, they first made the score and only afterward commissioned the words; thus the words and the pitches did not harmonize with each other, and the music differed little from popular tunes.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chongning era the court reversed the order—score first, lyrics later—so text and pitch fell out of step and the result scarcely differed from popular music.

sentences.zh: 乞復用古製。

translations.literal: I beg that the ancient system be restored.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we restore the ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮》奏黃鍾、歌大呂以祀天神。

translations.literal: Further, according to the Rites of Zhou, they play the Yellow Bell and sing the Great Clarity to sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also prescribe playing the Yellow Bell and singing the Great Clarity when sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾，堂下之樂；

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell is music for below the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell is the music of the lower hall;

sentences.zh: 大呂，堂上之樂也。

translations.literal: the Great Clarity is music for above the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Great Clarity is the music of the upper hall.

sentences.zh: 郊祀之禮，皇帝版位在午階下，故還位之樂當奏黃鍾；

translations.literal: In the suburban sacrifice, the emperor's position on the spirit tablet is below the Wu steps; therefore the music when returning to position should play the Yellow Bell;
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban altar the emperor's tablet stands below the Wu steps, so the return-to-position music should use Yellow Bell;

sentences.zh: 明堂版位在阼階上，則還位當歌大呂。

translations.literal: at the Bright Hall the tablet position is on the eastern steps above, and the return-to-position music should therefore sing the Great Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: at the Bright Hall the tablet stands on the upper eastern steps, so the return music should sing Great Clarity.

sentences.zh: 今明堂禮不下堂，而襲郊祀還位例，並奏黃鍾之樂，於義未當。

translations.literal: Now in the Bright Hall rite the emperor does not descend from the hall, yet they follow the suburban sacrifice precedent for returning to position and play only Yellow Bell music throughout—this is not appropriate in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Bright Hall rite never takes the emperor below the hall, yet we still follow the suburban return precedent and play only Yellow Bell throughout—which misapplies the rite.

sentences.zh: ”尋皆如普議。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward all were done as Pu had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court soon adopted all of Pu's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝嚐以時難備物，禮有從宜，敕戒有司參酌損益，務崇簡儉。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had once, because of the difficulty of the times in preparing full accoutrements, noted that rites allow adaptation to circumstances, and charged the relevant offices to weigh reductions and additions, striving above all for simplicity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ruled that hard times justified simplified rites: ministries should weigh what to cut or keep and favor austerity.

sentences.zh: 仍權依元年例，令登歌通作宮架，其押樂、舉麾官及樂工器服等，蠲省甚多。

translations.literal: They still provisionally followed the first-year precedent, having ascent music also serve as the palace frame; the music supervisors, banner-raisers, musicians' instruments and costumes, and the like were greatly reduced and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: They still followed the first-year expedient of letting ascent music double for the palace frame, and slashed supervisors, banner officers, instruments, costumes, and supporting staff.

sentences.zh: 既而國步漸安，始以保境息民為務，而禮樂之事浸以興矣。

translations.literal: Afterward, as the fortunes of the state gradually stabilized, they first made securing the borders and giving the people rest their task, and matters of rites and music gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm slowly stabilized, the court turned to securing borders and easing the people, and ritual music began to revive.

sentences.zh: 十年，太常卿蘇攜言：“將來明堂行禮，除登歌大樂已備，見闕宮架、樂舞，諸路州軍先有頒降登歌大樂，乞行搜訪應用。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Director of Imperial Sacrifices Su Xi said: "For the coming Bright Hall ceremony, aside from ascent music and great music already prepared, the palace frame and ritual dances are still lacking. Various circuits and prefectures and armies have previously been issued ascent music and great music; I beg that a search be conducted to supply what is needed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Director Su Xi reported: "For the upcoming Bright Hall rite, ascent music and great music are ready, but the palace frame and dances are still missing. Many circuits already hold issued ascent and great music—please search them out for use."

sentences.zh: ”丞周執羔言：“大樂兼用文、武二舞，今殿前司將下任道，係前大晟府二舞色長，深知舞儀，宜令赴寺教習。

translations.literal: " Assistant Director Zhou Zhigao said: "Great music uses both the civil and martial dances. Now the Palace Front Service officer Ren Dao, who was formerly a dance-section chief of the two dances in the Great Sheng Bureau, knows dance ritual thoroughly; he should be ordered to come to the directorate for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Assistant Director Zhou Zhigao added: "Great music requires both civil and martial dances. Ren Dao of the Palace Front Service, a former chief of the Great Sheng Bureau's dance sections, knows the choreography well—he should be sent to the directorate to train the dancers."

sentences.zh: ”卿陳桷言：“前期五使，例合按閱，仍詔應侍祠執事朝臣，並作樂教習。

translations.literal: " Director Chen Jue said: "The five commissioners of the preliminary period should, by precedent, conduct inspection, and an edict should also order all court officials who will attend the sacrifice in service to take part in music instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Director Chen Jue urged: "The five preliminary commissioners should inspect rehearsals as usual, and every court official scheduled to serve at the sacrifice should train with the musicians."

sentences.zh: ”禮儀博士周林復言：“神位席地陳設，至尊親行酌獻，堂上下皆地坐作樂，而鍾磬工乃設木小榻，當教習日，使立以考擊，庶革循習簡陋之弊。

translations.literal: " Ritual Doctor Zhou Linfu said: "The spirit tablets are set out on the ground; the sovereign in person performs the libation and offering; above and below the hall all perform music seated on the ground, yet the bell and stone workers set up small wooden couches—on rehearsal days they should be made to stand when striking for examination, so as to reform the habit of following crude and simplified practice.
translations.idiomatic: " Ritual Doctor Zhou Linfu noted: "Spirit tablets sit on the floor, the emperor pours the libation in person, and musicians above and below the hall perform seated on the ground—yet bell and stone players use low wooden stools. During rehearsals they should stand to strike, to break the habit of sloppy expedients."

sentences.zh: 初，上居諒闇，臣僚有請罷明堂行禮奏樂、受胙等事，上諭禮官詳定。

translations.literal: At first, while the emperor was in mourning seclusion, officials had requested suspending Bright Hall ceremonies, performing music, receiving sacrificial meat, and the like; the emperor instructed the ritual officials to examine and decide in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his mourning seclusion, officials asked to cancel Bright Hall music, sacrificial meat, and related observances; the emperor told the ritual offices to decide carefully.

sentences.zh: 太常寺檢照景德、熙、豐親郊典故，除郊廟、景靈宮並合用樂，其鹵簿、鼓吹及樓前宮架、諸軍音樂，皆備而不作。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices checked the precedents for imperial suburban sacrifices in the Jingde, Xining, and Yuanfeng periods: aside from suburban altars, ancestral temples, and the Jingling Palace, where music was used together, the processional guards, wind and percussion ensembles, palace frame before the tower, and music of the various armies were all prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Sacrifices reviewed Jingde, Xining, and Yuanfeng precedents for imperial suburban rites: music still accompanied suburban altars, ancestral temples, and Jingling Palace, but processions, wind ensembles, tower-frame music, and army bands were set out yet silenced.

sentences.zh: 每處警場，止鳴金鉦、鼓角而已，即無去奏樂、受胙之文。

translations.literal: At each warning ground only gongs, bells, and horns were sounded; there is no text about abolishing music performance or receiving sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: At each guard post only bronze gongs and horns sounded—nowhere do the precedents abolish ritual music or the sacrificial portion.

sentences.zh: 大饗為民祈福，為上帝、宗廟而作樂，禮不敢以卑廢尊。

translations.literal: The great offering seeks blessings for the people; music is made for the Supreme Lord and the ancestral temples—ritual does not dare to let the lower abolish the higher.
translations.idiomatic: The great feast blesses the people; music honors Heaven and the ancestors—rite must not let lesser mourning cancel what is supreme.

sentences.zh: 《書》“斂五福，錫庶民”，況熙寧禮尤可考，其赦文有曰“六樂備舞，祥祉來臻”是也。

translations.literal: The Documents says, "Gather the five blessings and bestow them on the multitude"; moreover the Xining rites are especially worth consulting—its amnesty text reads, "When the six kinds of music and dances are complete, auspicious blessings arrive," which is the point.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents promises to "gather the five blessings and grant them to the people"; the Xining rites are explicit, and an amnesty of that era declares, "With the six musics and dances complete, auspicious blessings arrive."

sentences.zh: 於是詔遵行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered that this be followed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed these rulings.

sentences.zh: 其後，禮部侍郎施奏：“禮經蕃樂出於荒政，蓋一時以示貶抑。

translations.literal: Afterward, Vice Minister of Rites Shi memorialized: "In the ritual classics, foreign music arose from misgovernment in border regions—it was only for a time, to show censure and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Minister of Rites Shi argued: "Ritual classics treat foreign music as a product of troubled border rule—a temporary mark of censure.

sentences.zh: 昨內外暫止用樂，今徽考大事既畢，慈寧又已就養，其時節上壽，理宜舉樂，一如舊制。

translations.literal: Yesterday music was temporarily suspended inside and outside the palace; now the great affairs for Emperor Huizong's posthumous honors are finished, and the Empress Dowager has already taken up residence for her maintenance at Cining; at this season of celebrating her longevity, it is reasonable to perform music, just as in the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Music was paused throughout the palace during the crisis; now Huizong's funeral rites are complete, the empress dowager has settled at Cining, and her birthday season warrants music as before."

sentences.zh: ”禮部尋言：“太母還宮，國家大慶，四方來賀。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Rites soon said: "The Grand Empress Dowager has returned to the palace—this is a great celebration for the state, and the four quarters come to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Rites added: "The grand empress dowager's return is a national celebration; envoys from every quarter will come to congratulate."

sentences.zh: 自今冬至、元正舉行朝賀之禮，依國朝故事，合設大仗及用樂舞等，庶幾明天子之尊，舊典不至廢墜。

translations.literal: From now on, for the winter solstice and New Year's Day, when conducting the court congratulation rites, according to our dynasty's precedents, the great guard array and the use of music and dance should be set up, so that the Son of Heaven's dignity may be made clear and old institutions not fall into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: From this winter solstice and New Year onward, court congratulations should follow dynastic precedent—grand guard arrays, music, and dance—so the Son of Heaven's dignity is visible and old forms are not lost."

sentences.zh: ”有詔俟來年舉行。

translations.literal: " There was an edict to wait until the following year to carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered these observances deferred until the next year.

sentences.zh: 十有三年，郊祀，詔以祐陵深弓劍之藏，長樂遂晨昏之養，昭答神天，就臨安行在所修建圓壇。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, for the suburban sacrifice, an edict stated that because the bow and sword of Youling lie buried deep, and perpetual joy in morning and evening nurture is now secured, to make clear response to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, a round altar was built at the traveling palace in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, for the suburban sacrifice, the court proclaimed that with Huizong laid to rest and the empress dowager cared for day and night, Heaven and Earth should be answered properly—and a round altar was built at the Lin'an temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 於是有司言：“大禮排設備樂，宮架樂辦一料外，登歌樂依在京夏祭例，合用兩料。

translations.literal: Thereupon the relevant offices said: "For the great ceremony's arrangement and full provision of music, aside from one set of palace-frame music, ascent music, following the capital's summer-sacrifice precedent, should use two sets in all.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "For the great rite we need a full music establishment: one palace-frame set plus two ascent-music sets, following the capital's summer-sacrifice precedent."

sentences.zh: 其樂器，登歌則用編鍾、磬各一架，、二，搏拊、鼓二，琴五色，自一、三、五、七至九糸玄各二，瑟四，笛四，塤、篪、簫並二，巢笙、和笙各四；

translations.literal: The instruments: for ascent music, use one rack of tuned bells and one of stone chimes; sounding blocks and hand drums, two each; zithers in the five colors, from one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string black each two; se, four; flutes, four; xun, chi, and xiao, two each; nest-sheng and he-sheng, four each;
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music requires one rack of bells and one of chimes; sounding blocks and hand drums, two each; colored zithers (one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string black), two of each; four se, four flutes, two each of xun, chi, and xiao; four nest-sheng and four he-sheng;

sentences.zh: 並七星、九曜、閏餘匏笙各一，麾幡一。

translations.literal: also one each of the Seven Stars, Nine Luminaries, and intercalary-surplus gourd-sheng, and one command banner.
translations.idiomatic: plus one each of the Seven Stars, Nine Luminaries, and intercalary gourd-sheng pipes, and one command banner.

sentences.zh: 宮架則用編鍾、編磬各十二架，、二，琴五色，各十，瑟二十六；

translations.literal: For the palace frame, use twelve racks of tuned bells and twelve of stone chimes; sounding blocks and hand drums, two each; zithers in the five colors, ten each; se, twenty-six;
translations.idiomatic: The palace frame needs twelve bell racks and twelve chime racks; sounding blocks and hand drums, two each; ten zithers in each of the five colors; twenty-six se;

sentences.zh: 巢笙及簫並一十四，七星、九曜、閏餘匏笙各一，竽笙十，塤一十二，篪一十八，笛二十，晉鼓一，建鼓四，麾幡一。

translations.literal: nest-sheng and xiao together fourteen; Seven Stars, Nine Luminaries, and intercalary-surplus gourd-sheng, one each; yu-sheng, ten; xun, twelve; chi, eighteen; flutes, twenty; Jin drum, one; establishment drums, four; command banner, one.
translations.idiomatic: fourteen nest-sheng and xiao combined; one each of the Seven Stars, Nine Luminaries, and intercalary gourd-sheng; ten yu-sheng; twelve xun; eighteen chi; twenty flutes; one Jin drum; four establishment drums; and one command banner.

sentences.zh: ”乃從太常下之兩浙、江南、福建州郡，又下之廣東西、荊湖南北，括取舊管大樂，上於行都，有闕則下軍器所製造，增修雅飾，而樂器浸備矣。

translations.literal: " Orders were then sent from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to the prefectures and circuits of Liang-Zhe, Jiangnan, and Fujian, and also to Guangdong, Guangxi, Jingxi, Hunan, and Hubei, to gather the great music formerly under their jurisdiction and send it up to the traveling capital; where anything was lacking, orders went to the Armory Workshop to manufacture, with elegant ornament added and repaired, and the instruments gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: " Imperial Sacrifices ordered Liang-Zhe, Jiangnan, Fujian, Lingnan, and Jing-Hu circuits to send stored great music to the capital; gaps were filled by the Armory Workshop, instruments were refurbished, and the ensemble slowly became complete.

sentences.zh: 其樂工，詔依太常寺所請，選擇行止畏謹之人，合登歌、宮架凡用四百四十人，同日分詣太社、太稷、九宮貴神。

translations.literal: As for the musicians, an edict followed what the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had requested: persons of cautious conduct and deportment were selected; for ascent music and palace frame together four hundred forty persons were used, and on the same day they were divided to go to the Altars of Soil and Grain and the Nine Palaces of the Noble Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians, as Imperial Sacrifices requested, were chosen for prudent conduct: 440 for ascent and palace-frame music, dispatched the same day to the altars of Soil and Grain and the Nine Palaces of the Noble Spirits.

sentences.zh: 每祭各用樂正二人，執色樂工、掌事、掌器三十六人，三祭共一百一十四人，文舞、武舞計用一百二十八人，就以文舞番充。

translations.literal: For each sacrifice two music directors were used; musicians holding colors, stewards, and instrument keepers, thirty-six persons—for the three sacrifices one hundred fourteen in all; civil and martial dances were reckoned at one hundred twenty-eight persons, and the civil dance rotations were used to fill this number.
translations.idiomatic: Each sacrifice employed two music directors, thirty-six color-musicians, stewards, and instrument keepers (114 across three rites), and 128 dancers for civil and martial pieces—the civil dance rotations supplied the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 其二舞引頭二十四人，皆召募補之。

translations.literal: The twenty-four dance leaders for the two dances were all recruited to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four dance leaders for the two dances were recruited to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 樂工、舞師照在京例，分三等廩給。

translations.literal: Musicians and dance masters, following the capital precedent, were given grain rations in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians and dance masters received grain stipends in three grades, following the capital precedent.

sentences.zh: 其樂正、掌事、掌器，自六月一日教習；

translations.literal: The music directors, stewards, and instrument keepers began instruction on the first day of the sixth month;
translations.idiomatic: Music directors, stewards, and instrument keepers began rehearsals on the first day of the sixth month;

sentences.zh: 引舞、色長、文武舞頭、舞師及諸樂工等，自八月一日教習。

translations.literal: dance leaders, color chiefs, civil and martial dance heads, dance masters, and all the musicians, and the like, began instruction on the first day of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: dance leaders, color chiefs, civil and martial dance captains, dance masters, and the remaining musicians began on the first day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 於是樂工漸集。

translations.literal: Thereupon the musicians gradually assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians gradually gathered.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太常寺言：“將來大禮，見闕玉磬十六枚。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "For the coming great ceremony, sixteen jade chime-stones are still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Sixteen jade chime-stones are still missing for the great rite."

sentences.zh: 其所定聲律，係於玉分厚薄，取聲高下。

translations.literal: The pitch standards fixed for them depend on the thickness of each slice of jade, by which high and low sound is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Their pitches depend on the thickness of each jade slice, which sets the tone high or low.

sentences.zh: 正聲凡十有二，黃鍾厚八分，進而為大呂、太簇、夾鍾、姑洗、仲呂、蕤賓、林鍾、夷則、南呂、無射、應鍾，每律增一分，至應鍾一寸九分而止。

translations.literal: The proper tones are twelve in all: Yellow Bell is eight fen thick; advancing through Great Clarity, Great Cluster, Pinched Bell, Maiden Wash, Second Clarity, Flaming Guest, Forest Bell, Levelizing Rule, Southern Clarity, Tireless Shot, and Responding Bell, each pitch adds one fen, stopping at Responding Bell at one cun and nine fen.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve standard tones begin with Yellow Bell at eight fen thick; each successive pitch—Great Clarity through Responding Bell—adds one fen, ending at one cun nine fen for Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 清聲夾鍾厚二寸三分，退而為太簇、大呂、黃鍾，共四清聲，各減一分，至黃鍾二寸而止。

translations.literal: For the clear tones, Pinched Bell is two cun and three fen thick; retreating through Great Cluster, Great Clarity, and Yellow Bell, four clear tones in all, each reduces by one fen, stopping at Yellow Bell at two cun.
translations.idiomatic: The four clear tones start with Pinched Bell at two cun three fen; stepping back through Great Cluster, Great Clarity, and Yellow Bell, each loses one fen until Yellow Bell reaches two cun.

sentences.zh: ”乃下之四川茶馬司，寬數增分，市易以供用。

translations.literal: " Orders were then sent to the Sichuan Tea-and-Horse Commission to allow extra quantities and added thicknesses and to purchase and exchange to supply use.
translations.idiomatic: " Orders went to the Sichuan Tea-and-Horse Commission to procure extra stone with generous tolerances for thickness.

sentences.zh: 太常博士張晟又言：“大樂所用武舞之飾，以幹配刀，《周禮·司兵》‘祭祀，授舞者兵’，先儒謂‘授以朱幹、玉戚’，《郊特牲》‘朱幹、玉戚，冕而舞大武’。

translations.literal: Ritual Doctor Zhang Sheng of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices also said: "The adornments used in the martial dance of great music pair a shield with a blade. In the Rites of Zhou, Director of Arms: 'At sacrifices, give the dancers weapons'—earlier scholars said 'give them vermilion shields and jade axes'; in the Record of Suburban Sacrifice, 'With vermilion shields and jade axes, capped and robed, they dance the Great Martial.'
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Doctor Zhang Sheng added: "Martial dance regalia pairs shield with blade. The Rites of Zhou's Director of Arms says sacrifices arm the dancers; earlier commentators specify vermilion shields and jade axes, as the Record of Suburban Sacrifice describes for the Great Martial dance."

sentences.zh: ”乃從所請，仿《三禮圖》，令造玉戚，以配舞幹。

translations.literal: " His request was followed; following the Illustrations of the Three Rites, orders were given to make jade axes to pair with the dance shields.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed and, following the Illustrations of the Three Rites, ordered jade axes made to accompany the dance shields.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始上徽宗徽號，特製《顯安之樂》。

translations.literal: That year, when they first presented the honorific title for Emperor Huizong, they specially composed the music "Manifest Peace."
translations.idiomatic: That year, when Huizong's honorific title was first presented, the court composed the hymn "Manifest Peace."

sentences.zh: 至於奉皇太后冊、寶於慈寧宮，樂用《聖安》；

translations.literal: As for presenting the empress dowager's patent of investiture and seal at the Cining Palace, the music used was "Sagely Peace";
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager's patent and seal were presented at Cining Palace, the music was "Sagely Peace";

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊、寶於穆清殿，樂用《坤安》，亦皆先後參次而舉。

translations.literal: when the empress received her patent and seal at the Muqing Hall, the music used was "Earthly Peace"—all were performed in due sequence according to precedence.
translations.idiomatic: when the empress received hers at Muqing Hall, the music was "Earthly Peace"—each performed in proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 《顯安》以無射、夾鍾為宮，《周大司樂》饗先王，奏無射而歌夾鍾，“夾鍾之六五，上生無射之上九。

translations.literal: "Manifest Peace" takes Tireless Shot and Pinched Bell as its tonal center. In the Zhou Grand Director of Music, when feasting the former kings, they play Tireless Shot and sing Pinched Bell: "Pinched Bell's six-fifths generates above to Tireless Shot's upper nine.
translations.idiomatic: "Manifest Peace" uses Tireless Shot and Pinched Bell as its tonal center. The Zhou Grand Director of Music plays Tireless Shot and sings Pinched Bell when feasting former kings: "Pinched Bell's six-fifths generates Tireless Shot's upper ninth."

sentences.zh: 夾鍾，卯之氣，二月建焉，而辰在降婁；

translations.literal: Pinched Bell is the qi of mao, established in the second month, and the chronogram is in Descending Harvest;
translations.idiomatic: Pinched Bell belongs to mao's qi, the second month, with the chronogram in Descending Harvest;

sentences.zh: 無射，戌之氣，九月建焉，而辰在大火。

translations.literal: Tireless Shot is the qi of xu, established in the ninth month, and the chronogram is in Great Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Tireless Shot belongs to xu's qi, the ninth month, with the chronogram in Great Fire.

sentences.zh: ”無射，陽律之終，夾鍾實為之合，蓋取其相親合而萃祖考之精神於假廟也。

translations.literal: " Tireless Shot is the end of the yang pitches; Pinched Bell is truly its mate—this takes their mutual kinship and union to gather the spirits of the ancestors and fathers in the temporary temple.
translations.idiomatic: " Tireless Shot ends the yang pitches; Pinched Bell pairs with it—drawing their affinity to gather ancestral spirits in the temporary temple.

sentences.zh: 《聖安》純用大呂，《坤安》純用中呂。

translations.literal: "Sagely Peace" uses only Great Clarity; "Earthly Peace" uses only Middle Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: "Sagely Peace" uses only Great Clarity; "Earthly Peace" uses only Middle Clarity.

sentences.zh: 大呂，陰律之首，崇母儀也；

translations.literal: Great Clarity is the head of the yin pitches—honoring the mother's ritual status;
translations.idiomatic: Great Clarity heads the yin pitches, honoring the mother;

sentences.zh: 中呂，陰律之次，明婦順也。

translations.literal: Middle Clarity is the second of the yin pitches—making clear the wife's obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Clarity is second among yin pitches, marking the wife's proper deference.

sentences.zh: 明年正旦朝會，始陳樂舞，公卿奉觴獻壽。

translations.literal: The next year at the New Year's Day court assembly, music and dance were first arrayed; dukes and ministers presented goblets and offered longevity wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year's court assembly restored music and dance; ministers presented cups and offered longevity wishes.

sentences.zh: 據元豐朝會樂：第一爵，登歌奏《和安之曲》，堂上之樂隨歌而發；

translations.literal: According to the Yuanfeng court-assembly music: for the first round, ascent music performs the tune "Harmonious Peace," and the music above the hall follows the song in sounding;
translations.idiomatic: Following Yuanfeng court-assembly music: at the first round, ascent music plays "Harmonious Peace," with upper-hall instruments following the vocal line;

sentences.zh: 第二爵，笙入，乃奏瑞曲，惟吹笙而餘樂不作；

translations.literal: for the second round, sheng enter, and then auspicious tunes are played—only the sheng are blown and the other music is not performed;
translations.idiomatic: at the second round, sheng enter and auspicious tunes sound—sheng alone, all else silent;

sentences.zh: 第三爵，奏瑞曲，堂上歌，堂下笙，一歌一吹相間；

translations.literal: for the third round, auspicious tunes are played—song above the hall, sheng below the hall, one song and one blowing alternating;
translations.idiomatic: at the third round, auspicious tunes alternate—vocal above, sheng below, song and pipe answering each other;

sentences.zh: 第四爵，合樂仍奏瑞曲，而上下之樂交作。

translations.literal: for the fourth round, combined music still plays auspicious tunes, and the music above and below performs together.
translations.idiomatic: at the fourth round, full ensemble plays the auspicious tunes, upper and lower music together.

sentences.zh: 今悉仿舊典，首奏《和安》，次奏《嘉木成文》、《滄海澄清》、《瑞粟呈祥》三曲，其樂專以太簇為宮。

translations.literal: Now all follow the old canon: first perform "Harmonious Peace," then the three tunes "Fine Timber Forms Pattern," "Blue Sea Clears," and "Auspicious Grain Shows Blessing"; the music takes Great Cluster alone as its tonal center.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed the old canon: first "Harmonious Peace," then "Fine Timber Forms Pattern," "Blue Sea Clears," and "Auspicious Grain Shows Blessing," all centered on Great Cluster.

sentences.zh: 太簇之律，生氣湊達萬物，於三統為人正，於四時為孟春，故元會用之。

translations.literal: The pitch Great Cluster is the tone in which generating qi gathers and reaches the ten thousand things; in the three systems it is the human standard; in the four seasons it is early spring—therefore the yearly grand assembly uses it.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster gathers the generative qi of all things; in the three cosmic systems it marks humanity's standard, in the seasons early spring—hence its use at the grand New Year assembly.

sentences.zh: 時給事中段拂等討論景鍾制度，按《大晟樂書》：“黃鍾者，樂所自出，而景鍾又黃鍾之本，故為樂之祖，惟天子郊祀上帝則用之，自齋宮詣壇則擊之，以召至陽之氣。

translations.literal: At that time Supervising Secretary Duan Fu and others discussed the institution of the Spectacular Bell. According to the Great Sheng Music Book: "Yellow Bell is where music issues from, and the Spectacular Bell is again the root of Yellow Bell—therefore it is the ancestor of music. Only when the Son of Heaven sacrifices to the Supreme Lord at the suburban altar is it used; from the fasting palace proceeding to the altar it is struck, to summon the utmost yang qi.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Duan Fu and others then debated the Spectacular Bell. The Great Sheng Music Book states: "Yellow Bell is music's source; the Spectacular Bell is Yellow Bell's root—the ancestor of music. Only the Son of Heaven uses it when sacrificing to Heaven at the suburban altar; it is struck leaving the fasting palace to summon the fullest yang qi."

sentences.zh: 既至，聲闋，眾樂乃作。

translations.literal: Once arrival is achieved, the sound ceases and the multitude of music then begins.
translations.idiomatic: When the altar is reached the bell falls silent and the full ensemble begins.

sentences.zh: 祀事既畢，升輦，又擊之。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice is finished and he ascends the palanquin, it is struck again.
translations.idiomatic: After the rite, as the emperor mounts his palanquin, it is struck again.

sentences.zh: 蓋天者，群物之祖，今以樂之祖感之，則天之百神可得而禮。

translations.literal: Heaven is the ancestor of the multitude of things; now using the ancestor of music to move it, then Heaven's hundred spirits may be obtained and ritually honored.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is ancestor to all things; striking music's ancestor moves Heaven, and its myriad spirits may be properly honored.

sentences.zh: 音韻清越，拱以九龍，立於宮架之中，以為君圍；

translations.literal: Its tone is clear and penetrating; arched by nine dragons, it stands in the midst of the palace frame as the sovereign's enclosure;
translations.idiomatic: Its tone is clear and far-reaching; nine dragons arch over it as it stands at the palace frame's center—the sovereign's ring;

sentences.zh: 環以四清聲鍾、磬、鎛鍾、特磬，以為臣圍；

translations.literal: ringed by the four clear-tone bells, chimes, bo bells, and special chimes, as the ministers' enclosure;
translations.idiomatic: ringed by the four clear-tone bells, chimes, bo bells, and special chimes as the ministers' ring;

sentences.zh: 編鍾、編磬以為民圍。

translations.literal: racks of bells and chimes form the people's enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: racked bells and chimes form the people's ring.

sentences.zh: 內設寶鍾球玉，外為龍虡鳳琴。

translations.literal: Inside are set precious bells, spheres, and jade; outside are dragon, tiger, and phoenix forms.
translations.idiomatic: Inside sit precious bells, spheres, and jade; outside dragon, tiger, and phoenix adorn it.

sentences.zh: 景鍾之高九尺，其數九九，實高八尺一寸。

translations.literal: The Spectacular Bell's height is nine chi—the number nine-nine—but in fact its height is eight chi and one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Spectacular Bell's nominal height is nine chi—the number nine-nine—but its actual height is eight chi one cun.

sentences.zh: 垂則為鍾，仰則為鼎。

translations.literal: Hanging down it is a bell; turned up it is a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Hanging down it is a bell; inverted it becomes a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 鼎之大，中於九斛，退藏實八斛有一焉。

translations.literal: The cauldron's capacity nominally hits nine hu; reduced and stored, in fact it is eight hu and one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Its cauldron capacity is nominally nine hu; measured inward, it holds eight hu and one sheng.

sentences.zh: ”內出皇祐大樂中黍尺，參以太常舊藏黃鍾律編鍾，高適九寸，正相吻合，遂遵用黍尺製造。

translations.literal: " From within came the millet measure from the Huangyou great music; compared with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' old stored Yellow Bell pitch rack of bells, the height matched nine cun exactly and truly aligned, and they therefore followed the millet measure in manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: " The court produced the Huangyou-era millet measure; compared with Imperial Sacrifices' stored Yellow Bell bell rack, nine cun matched exactly, and manufacture followed the millet measure."

sentences.zh: 鍾成，命左仆射秦檜為之銘。

translations.literal: When the bell was completed, the Left Vice Director Qin Hui was ordered to compose its inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When the bell was finished, Left Vice Director Qin Hui was commissioned to inscribe it.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：“皇宋紹興十六年，中興天子以好生大德，既定寰宇，乃作樂以暢天地之化，以和神人。

translations.literal: The text reads: "Great Song, sixteenth year of Shaoxing—the Restoring Son of Heaven, with his virtue of cherishing life, having already settled the realm, then made music to extend the transformation of Heaven and Earth and harmonize spirits and men.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription reads: "Great Song, Shaoxing year 16—the Restoring Son of Heaven, cherishing life, having settled the realm, made music to extend Heaven and Earth's transformation and harmonize spirits and humanity.

sentences.zh: 維茲景鍾，首出眾樂，天子專用禋祀，謹拜手稽首而獻銘。

translations.literal: This Spectacular Bell stands foremost among all music; the Son of Heaven alone uses it in the pure suburban sacrifice—I respectfully bow with joined hands, touch my forehead to the ground, and present this inscription.
translations.idiomatic: This Spectacular Bell leads all music; the Son of Heaven alone uses it in pure sacrifice to Heaven—I bow and present this inscription."

sentences.zh: 其銘曰：德純懿兮舜、文繼。

translations.literal: The inscription says: Virtue pure and excellent—Shun and Wen succeeded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The verse reads: Pure, excellent virtue—succession from Shun and King Wen.

sentences.zh: 躋壽域兮孰內外？

translations.literal: Who within or without does not enter the realm of longevity?
translations.idiomatic: Who within or without does not enter the realm of longevity?

sentences.zh: 薦上帝兮偉茲器。

translations.literal: Offering to the Supreme Lord—how grand is this vessel!
translations.idiomatic: Offered to the Supreme Lord—how grand this vessel!

sentences.zh: 聲氣應兮同久視。

translations.literal: Sound and qi respond—together long may he gaze!
translations.idiomatic: Sound and breath respond—long may he reign!

sentences.zh: 貽子孫兮彌萬世。

translations.literal: Bestowed on sons and grandsons—may it fill ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: Bestowed on sons and grandsons—for ten thousand generations!

sentences.zh: ”旋又命禮局造鎛鍾四十有八、編磬一百八十七、特磬四十八及添製編鍾等，命軍器所造建鼓八、雷鼓二、晉鼓一、雷鞀二、敔各四。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward orders went to the Ritual Bureau to make forty-eight bo bells, one hundred eighty-seven rack chimes, forty-eight special chimes, and additional tuned bell racks; the Armory Workshop was ordered to make eight establishment drums, two thunder drums, one Jin drum, two thunder nao, and four sounding-blocks each.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered the Ritual Bureau to cast forty-eight bo bells, 187 rack chimes, 48 special chimes, and supplemental bell racks; the Armory Workshop made eight establishment drums, two thunder drums, one Jin drum, two thunder nao, and four sounding-blocks apiece.

sentences.zh: 尋製金鍾、玉磬二架。

translations.literal: Soon afterward two racks of gold bells and jade chimes were made.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two racks of gold bells and jade chimes followed.

sentences.zh: 初，元豐本虞庭鳴球及晉賀循采玉造磬之義，命榮谘道肇造玉磬。

translations.literal: At first, in Yuanfeng, following the meaning of the sounding spheres in the Hall of Yu and Jin He Xun's gathering jade to make chimes, Rong Zidao was ordered to begin making jade chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanfeng, invoking the Hall of Yu's sounding spheres and Jin He Xun's jade-chime precedent, Rong Zidao was commissioned to begin the jade chimes.

sentences.zh: 元祐親祠，嚐一用之，久藏樂府。

translations.literal: At the imperial sacrifice in person in Yuanyou, they were once used; long stored in the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: They were used once at Yuanyou's imperial sacrifice, then stored long in the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 至政和加以磨礲，俾協音律，並造金鍾，專用於明堂。

translations.literal: By Zhenghe they were further polished and ground so as to harmonize with pitch standards, and gold bells were also made, used exclusively at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe they were polished to match the pitch standards; gold bells were cast for exclusive Bright Hall use.

sentences.zh: 蓋堂上之樂，歌鍾居左，歌磬居右。

translations.literal: For music above the hall, the song-bells stand on the left and the song-chimes on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In upper-hall music, song-bells stand left and song-chimes right.

sentences.zh: 金玉稟氣於乾，純精至貴，故鍾必以金，磬必以玉，始備金聲玉振之全，此中興所以繼作也。

translations.literal: Gold and jade receive their qi from Qian; pure essence is supremely precious—therefore bells must be of gold and chimes of jade, and only then is the fullness of golden sound and jade vibration complete; this is why the Restoration continued to make them.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and jade draw qi from Qian; as the purest essences, bells must be gold and chimes jade to achieve the full pairing of golden tone and jade resonance—the reason the Restoration revived them.

sentences.zh: 於是帝諭輔臣，以鍾磬音律，其餘皆和，惟黃鍾、大呂猶未應律，宜熟加考究。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor instructed his chief ministers that for the pitches of bells and chimes, all the rest were in harmony, but Yellow Bell and Great Clarity still did not respond to the standards—this should be studied thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers that bell and chime pitches were nearly aligned, but Yellow Bell and Great Clarity still missed the standard and needed thorough study.

sentences.zh: 詔禮官以鑄造鎛鍾，更須詳審，令聲和而律應，乃可奉祀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ritual officials that in casting the bo bells, still greater careful examination was required, so that sound would be harmonious and pitches responsive—only then could they be used in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials were ordered to cast the bo bells with extra care so tone and pitch matched before they could serve in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 命太常前期按閱，仍用皇祐進呈雅樂禮例。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to conduct preliminary inspection, still using the elegant-music ritual precedent presented in Huangyou.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Sacrifices was to inspect rehearsals beforehand, following the Huangyou elegant-music precedent.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御射殿，召宰執、侍從、台諫、寺監、館閣及武臣刺史以上，閱視新造景鍾及禮器。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the Archery Hall, summoned grand councilors, attendants, censorial and remonstrance officials, directorate and supervisory officials, academy and pavilion officials, and military officials of prefect rank and above, to review the newly made Spectacular Bell and ritual implements.
translations.idiomatic: At the Archery Hall the emperor summoned grand councilors, attendants, censors, supervisory officials, academicians, and prefect-rank military officers to inspect the new Spectacular Bell and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 皇帝即御坐，撞景鍾，用正旦朝會三曲，奏宮架之樂，其製造官推恩有差。

translations.literal: The emperor then took his seat, struck the Spectacular Bell, used the three tunes of the New Year's court assembly, and performed palace-frame music; the manufacturing officials received graded favors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat, struck the Spectacular Bell, played the three New Year court tunes with palace-frame music, and rewarded the craftsmen in graded ranks.

sentences.zh: 添置景鍾樂正一、鎛鍾樂工十有二，特磬樂工亦如之。

translations.literal: One music director for the Spectacular Bell was added, twelve musicians for the bo bells, and special-chime musicians in like number.
translations.idiomatic: The court added one Spectacular Bell director, twelve bo-bell musicians, and a matching staff for special chimes.

sentences.zh: 次降下古製銅錞一，增造其二；

translations.literal: Next an ancient-pattern bronze chun was issued down; two more were added;
translations.idiomatic: Next one ancient-pattern bronze chun was issued, with two more added;

sentences.zh: 古銅鐃一，增造其六。

translations.literal: one ancient bronze nao, with six more added.
translations.idiomatic: one ancient bronze nao, with six more added.

sentences.zh: 改造登歌夷則律玉磬，降到長笛二十有四，並付太常寺掌之，專俟大禮施用。

translations.literal: Ascent-music jade chimes in the Levelizing Rule pitch were refashioned; twenty-four long flutes were issued down—all entrusted to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to keep, reserved exclusively for use at the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent-music jade chimes in Levelizing Rule pitch were refitted; twenty-four long flutes were issued—all held by Imperial Sacrifices for the great ceremony alone.

sentences.zh: 既而刑部郎官許興古奏：“比歲休祥協應，靈芝產於廟楹，瑞麥秀於留都。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Ministry of Justice Bureau Director Xu Xinggu memorialized: "In recent years auspicious responses have aligned: lingzhi fungus grew on the temple pillars, and auspicious wheat flourished at the retained capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu Xinggu of the Ministry of Justice reported: "Auspicious omens have multiplied—lingzhi on temple pillars, auspicious wheat at the retained capital.

sentences.zh: 昔乾德六年，嚐詔和見作《瑞木》、《馴象》及《玉烏》、《皓雀》四瑞樂章，以備登歌。

translations.literal: Formerly in the sixth year of Qiande, an edict once ordered He Jian to compose the four auspicious hymn texts "Auspicious Timber," "Tamed Elephant," "Jade Crow," and "White Sparrow" for ascent music.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande year 6 the court once ordered He Jian to compose four auspicious hymns—"Auspicious Timber," "Tamed Elephant," "Jade Crow," and "White Sparrow"—for ascent music.

sentences.zh: 願依典故，製為樂章，登諸郊廟。

translations.literal: I wish, following precedent, to compose hymn texts and present them at suburban altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that new hymns be composed by precedent and entered into suburban and temple rites."

sentences.zh: ”詔從其請，命學士沈虛中作歌曲，以薦於太廟、圜丘、明堂。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his request and ordered Academician Shen Xuzhong to compose songs for offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Round Mound, and the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed and commissioned Academician Shen Xuzhong to write songs for the Imperial Temple, Round Mound, and Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋又內出御製郊祀大禮天地、宗廟樂章，及詔宰執、學士院、兩省官刪修郊祀大禮樂章，付太常肄習。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor also issued from within imperially composed hymn texts for the suburban sacrifice great ceremony to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, and ordered grand councilors, the Hanlin Academy, and officials of the two provincial secretariats to revise the suburban sacrifice great ceremony hymn texts, handing them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon issued his own suburban-sacrifice hymns for Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, ordered councilors, Hanlin academicians, and secretariat officials to revise them, and handed them to Imperial Sacrifices for rehearsal.

sentences.zh: 天子親祀南郊，圜鍾為宮，三奏，樂凡六成，歌《景安》，用《文德武功》之舞；

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven in person sacrificed at the southern suburb, Round Bell was the tonal center, three performances; music in all six sections; they sang "Manifest Peace" and used the dances "Civil Virtue" and "Martial Achievement";
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's southern suburban sacrifice, Round Bell served as tonal center with three performances and six musical sections; they sang "Manifest Peace" and danced "Civil Virtue" and "Martial Achievement";

sentences.zh: 饗明堂，夾鍾為宮，三奏，樂凡九成，歌《誠安》，用《佑文化俗》、《威功睿德之舞》。

translations.literal: at the Bright Hall feast, Pinched Bell was the tonal center, three performances, music in all nine sections; they sang "Sincere Peace" and used the dances "Aid Culture and Transform Custom" and "Majestic Merit and Sagely Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: at the Bright Hall feast, Pinched Bell was tonal center with three performances and nine sections; they sang "Sincere Peace" and danced "Aid Culture and Transform Custom" and "Majestic Merit and Sagely Virtue."

sentences.zh: 前二日，朝獻景靈宮，圜鍾為宮，三奏，凡六成，所奏樂與南郊同，歌《興安》，用《發祥流慶》、《降真觀德之舞》。

translations.literal: Two days before, at the morning offering to Jingling Palace, Round Bell was the tonal center, three performances, six sections in all; the music performed was the same as at the southern suburb; they sang "Rising Peace" and used the dances "Sending Blessings and Flowing Celebration" and "Descending Truth and Observing Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Two days earlier, at the Jingling Palace morning offering, Round Bell served as tonal center—three performances, six sections, the same music as the southern suburb; they sang "Rising Peace" and danced "Sending Blessings and Flowing Celebration" and "Descending Truth and Observing Virtue."

sentences.zh: 前一日，朝饗太廟，黃鍾為宮，三奏，樂凡九成，歌《興安》，所用文、武二舞與南郊同。

translations.literal: One day before, at the morning feast at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Yellow Bell was the tonal center, three performances, music in all nine sections; they sang "Rising Peace"; the civil and martial dances used were the same as at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, at the Imperial Temple morning feast, Yellow Bell was tonal center—three performances, nine sections; they sang "Rising Peace" with the same civil and martial dances as the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 僖祖廟用《基命之樂舞》，翼祖廟用《大順之樂舞》，宣祖廟用《天元之樂舞》，太祖廟用《皇武之樂舞》，太宗廟用《大定之樂舞》。

translations.literal: The temple of the Remote Ancestor used the music-dance "Foundation Mandate"; the temple of the Soaring Ancestor used "Great Accord"; the temple of the Proclaiming Ancestor used "Heaven's Origin"; the temple of the Grand Ancestor used "Imperial Martial"; the temple of the Exalted Ancestor used "Great Settlement."
translations.idiomatic: The Remote Ancestor's temple used "Foundation Mandate"; the Soaring Ancestor's, "Great Accord"; the Proclaiming Ancestor's, "Heaven's Origin"; Taizu's, "Imperial Martial"; Taizong's, "Great Settlement."

sentences.zh: 真宗、仁宗廟樂舞曰《熙文》、曰《美成》，英宗、神宗廟樂舞曰《治隆》、曰《大明》，哲宗、徽宗、欽宗廟樂舞曰《重光》、曰《承元》、曰《端慶》，皆以無射宮奏之。

translations.literal: The temples of Zhenzong and Renzong had music-dances called "Glorious Pattern" and "Beautiful Completion"; Yingzong and Shenzong, "Ordered Ascent" and "Great Brightness"; Zhezong, Huizong, and Qinzong, "Double Radiance," "Receiving Origin," and "Upright Celebration"—all performed in the Tireless Shot tonal center.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong and Renzong used "Glorious Pattern" and "Beautiful Completion"; Yingzong and Shenzong, "Ordered Ascent" and "Great Brightness"; Zhezong, Huizong, and Qinzong, "Double Radiance," "Receiving Origin," and "Upright Celebration"—all in the Tireless Shot tonal center.

sentences.zh: 每歲祀昊天上帝者凡四：正月上辛祈穀，孟夏雩祀，季秋饗明堂，冬至祀圜丘是也。

translations.literal: Each year sacrifices to the Supreme Lord of the Vast Heaven number four in all: the first upper xin day of the first month for praying for grain, the mid-summer rain prayer, the autumn Bright Hall feast, and the winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound—these are they.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was worshipped four times yearly: the first-month xin day for grain, mid-summer rain prayer, autumn Bright Hall feast, and winter solstice at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 圜鍾為宮，樂奏六成，與南郊同，乃用《景安之歌》、《帝臨嘉至》、《神矣錫羨之舞》。

translations.literal: Round Bell was the tonal center, music in six sections, the same as at the southern suburb; they used the song "Manifest Peace," and the dances "The Emperor Approaches in Auspicious Arrival" and "The Spirits Have Bestowed Blessings."
translations.idiomatic: Round Bell served as tonal center with six sections, as at the southern suburb; they sang "Manifest Peace" and danced "The Emperor Approaches in Auspicious Arrival" and "The Spirits Have Bestowed Blessings."

sentences.zh: 祀地祗者二：夏至祀皇地祗，樂奏八成，乃用《寧安之歌》、《儲靈錫慶》、《嚴恭將事之舞》；

translations.literal: Sacrifices to earthly spirits number two: at the summer solstice they sacrifice to the Imperial Earth Spirit, music in eight sections, using the song "Tranquil Peace" and the dances "Stored Spirits Bestow Celebration" and "Solemn Respect in Performing the Rite";
translations.idiomatic: Earth spirits were worshipped twice: at the summer solstice for the Imperial Earth Spirit, with eight sections, the song "Tranquil Peace," and dances "Stored Spirits Bestow Celebration" and "Solemn Respect in Performing the Rite";

sentences.zh: 立冬後祀神州地祗，樂奏八成，歌《寧安》，與祀皇地祗同名而異曲，用《廣生儲祐》、《厚載凝福之舞》。

translations.literal: after the Start of Winter they sacrifice to the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land, music in eight sections, singing "Tranquil Peace"—the same name as for the Imperial Earth Spirit but a different tune—using the dances "Broad Generation and Stored Blessing" and "Thick Bearing and Gathered Fortune."
translations.idiomatic: after Start of Winter for the Divine Land Earth Spirit, eight sections, the same hymn title "Tranquil Peace" but a different tune, with dances "Broad Generation and Stored Blessing" and "Thick Bearing and Gathered Fortune."

sentences.zh: 孟春上辛祀感生帝，其歌《大安》，其樂舞則與歲祀昊天同。

translations.literal: On the upper xin day of early spring they sacrifice to the Spirit of Felt Generation; its song is "Great Peace," and its music and dance are the same as the yearly sacrifice to the Vast Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On early spring's upper xin day they worshipped the Spirit of Felt Generation with "Great Peace," using the same music and dance as the annual Heaven sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 三年一袷及時饗太廟，九成之樂、《興安之歌》，與大禮前事朝饗同，而用《孝熙昭德》、《禮洽儲祥之舞》。

translations.literal: The triennial collective feast and timely feast at the Imperial Ancestral Temple use music in nine sections and the song "Rising Peace," the same as the morning feast before the great ceremony, but with the dances "Filial Splendor and Manifest Virtue" and "Rites Harmonized and Blessings Stored."
translations.idiomatic: The triennial collective feast and regular temple feast used nine sections and "Rising Peace," as before the great ceremony, with dances "Filial Splendor and Manifest Virtue" and "Rites Harmonized and Blessings Stored."

sentences.zh: 太社、太稷用《寧安》，八成之樂，與歲祀地祗同。

translations.literal: The Grand Altars of Soil and Grain use "Tranquil Peace," music in eight sections, the same as the yearly sacrifice to earthly spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Altars of Soil and Grain used "Tranquil Peace" in eight sections, as in the annual earth-spirit rites.

sentences.zh: 至於親製讚宣聖及七十二弟子，以廣崇儒右文之聲；

translations.literal: As for hymns in praise of the Exalted Sage and the seventy-two disciples composed in person by the emperor, these broadened the voice of honoring Confucian learning and elevating culture;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also composed hymns praising Confucius and the seventy-two disciples, amplifying the court's esteem for learning;

sentences.zh: 親視學，行酌獻，定釋奠為大祀，用《凝安》，九成之樂。

translations.literal: he personally inspected the schools, performed the libation and offering, fixed the libation sacrifice as a great ceremony, using "Gathered Peace," music in nine sections.
translations.idiomatic: personally inspected the schools, poured the libation, elevated the libation sacrifice to a great rite with "Gathered Peace" in nine sections.

sentences.zh: 郡邑行事，則樂止三成。

translations.literal: When prefectures and districts performed the rites, music stopped at three sections.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and districts used only three sections.

sentences.zh: 他如親饗先農、親祀高禖，則敞壇壝、奏樂舞，按習於同文館、法惠寺。

translations.literal: Other cases, such as personally feasting the Former Farmer or personally sacrificing to the High Matron, opened the altar enclosures and performed music and dance, rehearsed at the Tongwen Hall and Fahui Temple.
translations.idiomatic: For personal feasts to the Former Farmer or sacrifices to the High Matron, open altars and full music and dance were rehearsed at Tongwen Hall and Fahui Temple.

sentences.zh: 親耕籍田，則據宣和舊制，陳設大樂，而引呈耒耜、護衛耕根車、儀仗鼓吹至以二千人為率。

translations.literal: For personally plowing the sacred field, they followed the Xuanhe old system, arrayed great music, and presented plows and hoes, escorted the plowing-root carriage, and deployed ceremonial guards and wind ensembles—up to two thousand men as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor's sacred-field plowing, following Xuanhe precedent, great music was arrayed with plows presented, the plowing-root carriage escorted, and ceremonial guards and wind ensembles—some two thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 先農樂用《靜安》；

translations.literal: For the Former Farmer the music used was "Still Peace";
translations.idiomatic: The Former Farmer rite used "Still Peace";

sentences.zh: 高禖樂用《景安》；

translations.literal: for the High Matron the music used was "Manifest Peace";
translations.idiomatic: the High Matron rite used "Manifest Peace";

sentences.zh: 皇帝親行三推禮，樂用《乾安》。

translations.literal: when the emperor in person performed the three-push rite, the music used was "Qian Peace."
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor performed the three-push plowing himself, the music was "Qian Peace."

sentences.zh: 其補苴軼典、蒐講彌文者至矣。

translations.literal: In patching lost canons and gathering and elaborating ritual texts, they had reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In restoring lost precedents and elaborating ritual texts, the court had gone as far as could be.

sentences.zh: 先朝凡雅樂皆以‘安’名，中興一遵用之。

translations.literal: In the former court all elegant music was named with "An" (Peace); the Restoration followed this entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier courts named all elegant music with "Peace"; the Restoration followed suit.

sentences.zh: 南郊樂，其宮圜鍾；

translations.literal: For southern-suburb music, its tonal center is Round Bell;
translations.idiomatic: Southern-suburb music used Round Bell as tonal center;

sentences.zh: 明堂樂，其宮夾鍾。

translations.literal: for Bright Hall music, its tonal center is Pinched Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall music used Pinched Bell.

sentences.zh: 圜鍾即夾鍾也。

translations.literal: Round Bell is Pinched Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Round Bell is Pinched Bell.

sentences.zh: 夾鍾生於房、心之氣，實為天帝之堂，故為天宮。

translations.literal: Pinched Bell is born from the qi of Fang and Xin; it is in truth the hall of the Heavenly Emperor—therefore it is the Heaven palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pinched Bell draws qi from Fang and Xin—the Heavenly Emperor's hall—hence the Heaven palace.

sentences.zh: 祭地祇，其宮函鍾，即林鍾也。

translations.literal: In sacrificing to earthly spirits, the tonal center is Enveloping Bell, which is Forest Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Earth-spirit sacrifice used Enveloping Bell—Forest Bell—as tonal center.

sentences.zh: 林鍾生於未之氣，未為坤位，而天社、地神實在東井、輿鬼之外，故為地宮。

translations.literal: Forest Bell is born from the qi of wei; wei is the Kun position, and the Heavenly Altar of Soil and earthly spirits in truth lie beyond Well and Ghost Carriage—therefore it is the Earth palace.
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell draws wei's qi; wei is Kun's position, and the altars of soil lie beyond Well and Ghost Carriage—hence the Earth palace.

sentences.zh: 饗宗廟，其宮用黃鍾。

translations.literal: In feasting at the ancestral temples, Yellow Bell is used as the tonal center.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple feasts used Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾生於虛、危之氣，虛、危為宗廟，故為人宮。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is born from the qi of Xu and Wei; Xu and Wei are the ancestral temples—therefore it is the Human palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell draws Xu and Wei's qi—the ancestral temples—hence the Human palace.

sentences.zh: 此三者，各用其聲類求之。

translations.literal: These three each seek their pitches according to their sound categories.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three derives its pitches from its own sound category.

sentences.zh: 然天宮取律之相次：圜鍾為陰聲第五，陰將極而陽生，故取黃鍾為角。

translations.literal: Yet the Heaven palace takes pitches in succession: Round Bell is the fifth yin pitch; yin is about to reach its extreme and yang is generated—therefore Yellow Bell is taken as the horn.
translations.idiomatic: The Heaven palace follows successive pitches: Round Bell is the fifth yin pitch; as yin nears its limit yang arises—so Yellow Bell serves as horn.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾，陽聲之首也。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is the head of the yang pitches.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell heads the yang pitches.

sentences.zh: 太簇，陽聲之第二，故太簇為徵。

translations.literal: Great Cluster is the second yang pitch—therefore Great Cluster is the trigger.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster is second among yang pitches—hence the trigger.

sentences.zh: 姑洗，陽聲之第三，故姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Maiden Wash is the third yang pitch—therefore Maiden Wash is the feather.
translations.idiomatic: Maiden Wash is third—hence the feather.

sentences.zh: 天道有自然之秩序，乃取其相次者以為聲。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven has a natural order; therefore they take those in succession to make sound.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way has natural order; successive pitches shape its sound.

sentences.zh: 地宮取律之相生：函鍾上生太簇，故太簇為角；

translations.literal: The Earth palace takes pitches in mutual generation: Enveloping Bell generates Great Cluster above—therefore Great Cluster is the horn;
translations.idiomatic: The Earth palace uses generating pitches: Enveloping Bell generates Great Cluster above—Great Cluster as horn;

sentences.zh: 太簇下生南呂，南呂上生姑洗，故南呂為徵，姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Great Cluster generates Southern Clarity below, and Southern Clarity generates Maiden Wash above—therefore Southern Clarity is the trigger and Maiden Wash the feather.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster generates Southern Clarity below; Southern Clarity generates Maiden Wash above—Southern Clarity as trigger, Maiden Wash as feather.

sentences.zh: 地道資生而不窮，乃取其相生者以為聲。

translations.literal: The Way of Earth supports generation without end; therefore they take those in mutual generation to make sound.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's Way endlessly nurtures life; generating pitches shape its sound.

sentences.zh: 人宮取律之相合：黃鍾子，大呂醜，故黃鍾為宮、大呂為角，子合醜也；

translations.literal: The Human palace takes pitches in mutual pairing: Yellow Bell is zi, Great Clarity is chou—therefore Yellow Bell is the palace tone and Great Clarity the horn; zi pairs with chou;
translations.idiomatic: The Human palace uses paired pitches: Yellow Bell is zi, Great Clarity chou—Yellow Bell as palace tone, Great Clarity as horn; zi pairs with chou;

sentences.zh: 太簇寅，應鍾亥，故太簇為徵、應鍾為羽，寅合亥也。

translations.literal: Great Cluster is yin, Responding Bell is hai—therefore Great Cluster is the trigger and Responding Bell the feather; yin pairs with hai.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster is yin, Responding Bell hai—Great Cluster as trigger, Responding Bell as feather; yin pairs with hai.

sentences.zh: 人道以合而相親，乃取其合者以為聲。

translations.literal: The Way of Humanity draws near through pairing; therefore they take those that pair to make sound.
translations.idiomatic: Humanity draws kin through pairing; paired pitches shape its sound.

sentences.zh: 周之降天神、出地示、禮人鬼，樂之綱要實在於此。

translations.literal: The Zhou sending down the spirits of Heaven, issuing forth the manifestations of Earth, and ritually honoring the ghosts of men—the guiding principles of music truly lie in this.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou rites of sending down Heaven's spirits, issuing Earth's manifestations, and honoring human ghosts—the music's guiding principles lie here.

sentences.zh: 獨商聲置而不用，蓋商聲剛而主殺，實鬼神之所畏也。

translations.literal: Only the Shang pitch was set aside and not used—for the Shang pitch is hard and governs killing; spirits and ghosts truly fear it.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Shang pitch was omitted—hard and governing killing, what spirits fear.

sentences.zh: 樂奏六成者，即仿周之六變，八成、九成亦如之。

translations.literal: Music in six sections imitates the Zhou six transformations; eight and nine sections follow the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Six musical sections imitate the Zhou six transformations; eight and nine sections follow likewise.

sentences.zh: 文、武二舞皆用八佾。

translations.literal: Both the civil and martial dances use eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: Both civil and martial dances used eight rows of dancers.

sentences.zh: 國初，始改《崇德之舞》曰《文德》，改《象成》之舞曰《武功》。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, they first changed the dance "Honoring Virtue" to "Civil Virtue," and the dance "Elephant Completion" to "Martial Achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty "Honoring Virtue" became "Civil Virtue" and "Elephant Completion" became "Martial Achievement."

sentences.zh: 其《發祥流慶》、《降真觀德》則祥符所製，以薦獻聖祖；

translations.literal: "Sending Blessings and Flowing Celebration" and "Descending Truth and Observing Virtue" were made in the Xiangfu period to offer to the Sagely Ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: "Sending Blessings and Flowing Celebration" and "Descending Truth and Observing Virtue" were composed in Xiangfu for the Sagely Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 其《佑文化俗》、《威功睿德》則皇祐所製，以奉明禋。

translations.literal: "Aid Culture and Transform Custom" and "Majestic Merit and Sagely Virtue" were made in Huangyou to serve the bright suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: "Aid Culture and Transform Custom" and "Majestic Merit and Sagely Virtue" were composed in Huangyou for the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其祀帝，有司行事，以《帝臨嘉至》、《神矣錫羨》，與夫獻太廟以《孝熙昭德》、《禮洽儲祥》，則製於元豐。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to the Thearch when officials performed the rite, "The Emperor Approaches in Auspicious Arrival" and "The Spirits Have Bestowed Blessings" were used; and for offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, "Filial Splendor and Manifest Virtue" and "Rites Harmonized and Blessings Stored" were made in Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Official sacrifices to Heaven used "The Emperor Approaches in Auspicious Arrival" and "The Spirits Have Bestowed Blessings"; temple offerings used "Filial Splendor and Manifest Virtue" and "Rites Harmonized and Blessings Stored"—both from Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 其《廣生儲祐》、《厚載凝福》以祀方澤，則製於宣和。

translations.literal: "Broad Generation and Stored Blessing" and "Thick Bearing and Gathered Fortune" for sacrificing at the square marsh-altar were made in Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: "Broad Generation and Stored Blessing" and "Thick Bearing and Gathered Fortune" for the square marsh-altar dated from Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 至紹興祀皇地祇，易以《儲靈錫慶》、《嚴恭將事》，而用宣和所製舞以分祀神州地祗，轉相緝熙，樂舞浸備。

translations.literal: By Shaoxing, in sacrificing to the Imperial Earth Spirit, they changed to "Stored Spirits Bestow Celebration" and "Solemn Respect in Performing the Rite," while using Xuanhe-made dances to divide sacrifice to the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land; turning and continuing in succession, music and dance gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaoxing, worship of the Imperial Earth Spirit switched to "Stored Spirits Bestow Celebration" and "Solemn Respect in Performing the Rite," while Xuanhe dances served the separate Divine Land rite—music and dance slowly reached completion.

sentences.zh: 至中興而賡續裁定，實集其成。

translations.literal: By the Restoration they continued and finalized it, truly gathering its completion.
translations.idiomatic: The Restoration continued and finalized the system, bringing it to completion.

sentences.zh: 中祀而下，多有樂而無舞，則在《禮》“凡小祭祀不興舞”之義也。

translations.literal: For medium sacrifices and below, many had music but no dance—this lies in the Rites' meaning that "for all minor sacrifices dance is not raised."
translations.idiomatic: Medium and lesser rites often had music without dance, following the Rites' rule that minor sacrifices do not raise dance.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年，有詔：教坊日下蠲罷，各令自便。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Shaoxing, there was an edict: the Music Bureau is abolished forthwith; each is to go his own way.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 31 an edict abolished the Music Bureau and released its members.

sentences.zh: 蓋建炎以來，畏天敬祖，虔恭祀事，雖禮樂煥然一新，然其始終常以天下為憂，而未嚐以位為樂，有足稱者。

translations.literal: From Jianyan onward, revering Heaven and honoring ancestors, devout in sacrificial affairs—though rites and music were brilliantly renewed, from first to last he constantly took the realm as his worry and never took the throne as his pleasure; this is worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianyan onward Gaozong revered Heaven and ancestors and restored ritual music, yet he always worried for the realm rather than reveling in power—worth commendation.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初踐大位，立班設仗於紫宸殿，備陳雅樂。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong first ascended the great throne, he formed ranks and set guards at the Purple Bright Hall, fully arraying elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong first took the throne, he formed court ranks and guards at the Purple Bright Hall with full elegant music.

sentences.zh: 禮官尋請車駕親行朝饗，用登歌、金玉大樂及彩繪宮架、樂舞；

translations.literal: Ritual officials soon requested that the imperial carriage in person conduct the morning feast, using ascent music, gold and jade great music, and painted palace-frame music and dance;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials soon asked the emperor to conduct the morning feast in person with ascent music, gold and jade great music, painted palace frame, and dance;

sentences.zh: 仗內鼓吹，以欽宗喪製不用。

translations.literal: Wind ensembles within the guard array were not used because of Qinzong's mourning regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Guard wind ensembles were omitted under Qinzong's mourning.

sentences.zh: 迨安穆皇后祔廟，禮部侍郎黃中首言：“國朝故事，神主升祔，係用鼓吹導引，前至太廟，乃用樂舞行事。

translations.literal: When Empress Anmu was enshrined in the ancestral temple, Vice Minister of Rites Huang Zhong was first to say: "By our dynasty's precedent, when a spirit tablet is elevated to collective enshrinement, wind ensembles are used to lead the way forward to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and only then is music and dance used in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Anmu was enshrined, Vice Minister Huang Zhong argued first: "Dynastic precedent uses wind ensembles to escort a spirit tablet to the Imperial Temple, then music and dance for the rite itself.

sentences.zh: 宗廟薦享雖可用樂，鼓吹施於道路，情所未安，請備而不作。

translations.literal: Though music may be used in ancestral temple offerings, applying wind ensembles on the road is what the feelings cannot accept—I beg that they be prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Temple offerings may use music, but wind ensembles on the road feel wrong—I ask they be prepared but not played."

sentences.zh: ”續下給、舍詳議，謂：“薦享宗廟，為祖宗也，故以大包小，則別廟不嫌於用樂。

translations.literal: " The Secretariat drafters and revisers deliberated in detail, saying: "Offerings at the ancestral temple are for the ancestors; therefore the greater encompasses the lesser, and separate temples need not scruple at using music.
translations.idiomatic: " Secretariat drafters replied: "Temple offerings honor the ancestors; the greater encompasses the lesser, so separate temples need not avoid music.

sentences.zh: 今祔廟之禮為安穆而行，豈可與薦享同日語？

translations.literal: The present enshrinement rite is performed for Anmu—how can it be spoken of in the same breath as offerings?
translations.idiomatic: Today's enshrinement is for Anmu—how can it be equated with regular offerings?

sentences.zh: 將來祔禮，謁祖宗諸室，當用樂舞；

translations.literal: In future enshrinement rites, when visiting the various chambers of the ancestors, music and dance should be used;
translations.idiomatic: Future enshrinements should use music and dance when visiting the ancestors' chambers;

sentences.zh: 至別廟奉安，宜停而不用。

translations.literal: but at the separate temple for installation and enshrinement, it is appropriate to stop and not use them.
translations.idiomatic: but at the separate installation temple, music should stop.

sentences.zh: 蓋用樂於前殿，是不以欽宗而廢祖宗之禮；

translations.literal: Using music in the front hall means not abolishing the ancestors' rites because of Qinzong;
translations.idiomatic: Music in the front hall preserves the ancestors' rites despite Qinzong's mourning;

sentences.zh: 停樂於別廟，是安穆為欽宗喪禮而屈也。

translations.literal: stopping music at the separate temple means Anmu yields to Qinzong's mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: silence at the separate temple shows Anmu yielding to Qinzong's mourning.

sentences.zh: 如此，則於禮順，於義允。

translations.literal: Thus ritual is orderly and principle is satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: This satisfies both ritual order and principle.

sentences.zh: ”遂俞其請。

translations.literal: " His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 既而右正言周操上言：“祖宗前殿，尊無二上，其於用樂，無復有嫌。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Right Remonstrance Official Zhou Cao memorialized: "In the front hall of the ancestors, honor admits no second above—there is no further scruple about using music.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Zhou Cao then argued: "In the ancestors' front hall, honor admits no rival—music should raise no scruple.

sentences.zh: 然用之享廟行禮之日則可，而用於今日之祔則不可。

translations.literal: Yet to use it on the day of performing the temple feast rite is acceptable; to use it for today's enshrinement is not.
translations.idiomatic: It may be used on regular temple feast days, but not for today's enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 蓋祔禮為安穆而設，則其所用樂是為安穆而用，雖曰停於別廟，而為祔後用樂之名猶在也。

translations.literal: The enshrinement rite is set up for Anmu—therefore the music used is used for Anmu; though one says it is stopped at the separate temple, the name of using music after enshrinement still remains.
translations.idiomatic: Enshrinement is for Anmu—any music serves her; stopping it at the separate temple still leaves the name of post-enshrinement music.

sentences.zh: 孰若前後殿樂俱不作為無可議哉？

translations.literal: How much better if music in both front and rear halls were not performed—then there would be nothing to dispute!
translations.idiomatic: Better to silence both halls entirely—then nothing remains to dispute.

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乾道改元，始郊見天地。

translations.literal: When the era name was changed to Qiandao, he first sacrificed at the suburbs and appeared before Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiandao era began, Xiaozong first sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 太常洪適奏：“聖上踐阼，務崇乾德，郊丘講禮，專以誠意交於神明。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Sacrifices Hong Shi memorialized: "Your Majesty has ascended the throne, striving to exalt the virtue of Qian; at the suburban mound and hill you expound the rites, focusing solely on sincerity in communing with the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Director Hong Shi reported: "Your Majesty, newly enthroned, exalts Qian's virtue and approaches the spirits with sincerity at the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 竊謂古今不相沿樂，金石八音不入俗耳，通國鮮習其藝，而聽之則倦且寐，獨以古樂嚐用之郊廟爾。

translations.literal: I venture to think that ancient and modern music do not follow one another; the eight tones of metal and stone do not enter popular ears—the whole state rarely practices this art, and hearing it one grows weary and falls asleep. Ancient music is used only at suburban altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern music do not follow one another; metal and stone tones weary popular ears—the realm scarcely practices them, and listeners grow drowsy. Ancient music is reserved for suburban altars and temples alone.

sentences.zh: 昔者，竽工、鼓員不應經法，孔光、何武嚐奏罷於漢代，前史是之。

translations.literal: Formerly, yu workers and drum officers did not accord with canonical law; Kong Guang and He Wu once memorialized to abolish them in the Han dynasty, and earlier histories approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu players and drum officers once violated canonical law; Kong Guang and He Wu memorialized to abolish them in Han, and historians approved.

sentences.zh: 今樂工為數甚夥，其鹵簿六引、前後鼓吹，有司已奏明，詔三分減一，惟是肄習尚逾三月之淹。
