translations.literal: Now the musicians in number are very many; as to the banner-guard six led processions and front and rear processional music, the relevant offices have already memorialized clearly, and an edict cut them by one-third—yet drill and practice still exceed a delay of three months.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians now number in the thousands; for banner escorts, six-fold led processions, and front and rear processional bands, the ministries have already reported, and the court ordered a one-third reduction—yet rehearsal still drags on past three months.

sentences.zh: 夫驅遊手之人振金擊石，安能盡中音律，使鳳儀而獸舞？

translations.literal: To drive idlers to strike metal and beat stone—how could they fully hit the pitch rules and make phoenixes posture and beasts dance?
translations.idiomatic: How can idle hands striking bells and stones ever hit every pitch and move phoenixes and beasts to dance?

sentences.zh: 而日給虛耗，總為緡錢近二钜萬。

translations.literal: Yet daily allowances are vainly consumed, totaling in strings of cash nearly twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Daily pay drains the treasury to nearly twenty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 若從裁酌，用一月教習，自可應聲合節，不至闕事。

translations.literal: If one follows trimming and deliberation, using one month to teach and drill, of itself one may respond to sound and match the beat, and not arrive at neglecting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With prudent cuts, one month of training would match pitch and rhythm without disrupting the rites.

sentences.zh: ”於是詔郊祀樂工，令肄習一月。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict ordered suburban-sacrifice musicians to drill for one month.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then limited suburban-sacrifice musicians to one month of practice.

sentences.zh: 太常寺復言：“郊祀合用節奏樂工、登歌宮架樂工、引舞舞工，其分詣社稷及別廟，並番輪應奉，更不添置。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices again said: "For suburban sacrifice, the combined use of cadence musicians, ascent-music and palace-frame musicians, and lead-dance dancers—in their assignments to the altars of soil and grain and separate temples, all rotate in turns to serve; none need be newly added.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices added: "Suburban rites need cadence bands, ascent-song and palace-frame players, and lead dancers; those posted to the soil-and-grain altars and branch temples already rotate on roster—no new hires are needed.

sentences.zh: ”尋以禮官裁減壇下宮架二百七人，省十之一；

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward the ritual officials trimmed and reduced the palace frame below the altar, two hundred seven persons, cutting one in ten;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers soon cut the altar's lower palace-frame staff from 207 by one-tenth;

sentences.zh: 琴二十人，瑟十二人，各省其半；

translations.literal: zithers twenty persons, se twelve persons, each cut by half;
translations.idiomatic: zithers from twenty to ten, se from twelve to six;

sentences.zh: 笙、簫、笛可省者十有八人；

translations.literal: sheng, xiao, and flutes—those who could be cut numbered eighteen persons;
translations.idiomatic: eighteen fewer on sheng, xiao, and flute;

sentences.zh: 篪、塤可省者十人。

translations.literal: chi and xun—those who could be cut numbered ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: ten fewer on chi and xun.

sentences.zh: 其分詣給祠凡一百十四，止用八十人。

translations.literal: Those assigned to supply sacrifices totaled one hundred fourteen; they used only eighty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Postings for branch sacrifices dropped from 114 to 80.

sentences.zh: 鍾、磬凡四十八架，止設三十有二人，其宮架鍾、磬仍舊。

translations.literal: Bells and chimes totaled forty-eight frames; they set up only thirty-two persons; the palace-frame bells and chimes remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bell and chime frames, forty-eight in all, were manned by thirty-two players; the palace-frame bells and chimes were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 排殿閑慢樂色量省人數，悉報如章。

translations.literal: For lining-the-hall slow leisurely music colors, they measured and cut the number of persons; all was reported according to the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Slow hall music was also trimmed, and everything was filed as proposed.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎官蕭國梁又言：“議禮者嚐援紹興指揮，時饗亞獻既入太室，即引終獻行事，雖便於有司侍祠，免至跛倚，而其流將至於簡。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites bureau official Xiao Guoliang also said: "Those discussing rites once cited Shaoxing directives: at seasonal feasts, once the subordinate offering had entered the Grand Chamber, they at once led the final offering to perform the rites—though convenient for the relevant officials attending sacrifice and avoiding leaning and lame movement, yet its drift would come to oversimplification.
translations.idiomatic: Rites official Xiao Guoliang objected: "Liturgists cite a Shaoxing order that, at seasonal feasts, once the subordinate offering enters the Grand Chamber, the final offering follows at once—convenient for attendants and avoiding awkward gaps, but it trends toward oversimplification.

sentences.zh: 宗廟用之郊饗尤為非宜。

translations.literal: To use this at ancestral temples and suburban feasts is especially not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: It is especially wrong for ancestral temples and suburban feasts.

sentences.zh: 蓋有獻必有樂，卒爵而後樂闋。

translations.literal: For where there is offering there must be music; only when the goblet is finished does music cease.
translations.idiomatic: Every offering demands its music; music ends only when the cup is drained.

sentences.zh: 今亞、終獻樂舞雖同，而其作有始，其成有終，不可亂也。

translations.literal: Now the subordinate and final offerings' music and dance, though the same, yet their performance has a beginning and their completion has an end—one cannot confuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate and final offerings may share the same dances, but each performance has its own beginning and end and must not be scrambled.

sentences.zh: 若使之相繼行事，雜然於酌獻之間，則其為樂舞者，不知亞獻之樂耶，終獻之樂耶？

translations.literal: If one makes them succeed one another in performing the rites, jumbled amid the libation offerings, then those who perform music and dance would not know whether it is the subordinate offering's music or the final offering's music?
translations.idiomatic: If they run back-to-back amid the libations, the dancers will not know whether they dance for the subordinate or the final offering.

sentences.zh: ”詔從其請訂定。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his request and fixed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his plea and fixed the order.

sentences.zh: 淳熙六年，始舉明堂禋禮，命五使按雅樂並嚴更、警場於貢院，奉詔將樂器依堂上、堂下儀製排設，五使及應赴官僚從旁立觀按閱，仍聽往來察視。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chunxi, they first conducted the Bright Hall suburban-sacrifice rite, ordering the Five Commissioners to rehearse elegant music and also rigorously change watches and warning ground at the tribute academy, receiving the edict to arrange musical instruments according to hall-above and hall-below ritual regulations; the Five Commissioners and officials who should attend stood at the side watching the inspection, and were still permitted to go back and forth to observe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1179, the court first held the Bright Hall rite. Five commissioners rehearsed elegant music and tightened watches and the warning ground at the tribute academy, lining instruments above and below the hall per statute while officials watched—and could move about to inspect.

sentences.zh: 時大禮使趙雄言：“前例，閱樂至皇帝詣飲福位一曲，即五使以下皆立，而每閱奠玉幣及酌獻等樂，皆坐自如，於禮未盡，不當襲用前例。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Ritual Commissioner Zhao Xiong said: "Former precedent: when rehearsing music, upon reaching the piece for the emperor's proceeding to the drinking-fortune position, the Five Commissioners and below all stood; yet each time rehearsing music for presenting jade disks and currency and libation offerings and the like, all sat as they pleased—this in rites is not complete; one should not follow the former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ritual Commissioner Zhao Xiong said: "In past rehearsals, when music reached the emperor's approach to the fortune-drinking station, the five commissioners and below all stood—but for music for jade, silk, and libation offerings they remained seated. That falls short of ritual decorum and should not be copied.

sentences.zh: ”故有是詔。

translations.literal: " Therefore there was this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the new order.

sentences.zh: 既而禮官討論，自紹興以來，凡五饗明堂，禮畢還輦，並未經用樂，即無作樂節次可考。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward ritual officials discussed: since Shaoxing, for all five Bright Hall feasts, when the rite was completed and the carriage returned, none had employed music—thus there were no music start-and-stop stages to examine.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers then noted that, since Shaoxing, none of five Bright Hall feasts had used music on the return procession—so no precedents existed for when music should start or stop.

sentences.zh: 乃參酌禮例，成禮稱賀及肆赦用樂導駕，並用皇祐大饗典故施行。

translations.literal: They then consulted and weighed ritual precedents; for completing the rite, offering congratulations, and proclaiming amnesty, using music to lead the imperial carriage—all employed the Huangyou Grand Feast old statutes to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: They drew on precedent: music for felicitations and amnesty escorting the imperial carriage followed the Huangyou Grand Feast regulations.

sentences.zh: 其南郊、明堂儀注，實述紹興成憲，又命有司兼酌元豐、大觀舊典，為後世法程。

translations.literal: Their Southern Suburb and Bright Hall ritual regulations in fact narrated the Shaoxing completed statutes; they again ordered the relevant offices concurrently to draw on Yuanfeng and Daguan old canons, as models for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Suburb and Bright Hall manuals chiefly codified Shaoxing practice while also drawing on Yuanfeng and Daguan canon as a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 其用樂作止之節，粲然可觀：

translations.literal: Their stages for using music, starting and stopping, were brilliantly clear to view:
translations.idiomatic: When music began and ceased was now lucid throughout:

sentences.zh: 前三日，太常設登歌樂於壇上，稍南，北向，設宮架於壇南內壝之外，立舞表於酂綴之間

translations.literal: Three days before, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set ascent music on the altar platform, slightly south, facing north; set the palace frame outside the inner moat south of the altar; erected dance markers between the Zan tassels
translations.idiomatic: Three days before, the Court set ascent music on the altar, slightly south and facing north; placed the palace frame beyond the inner moat on the altar's south side; and set dance markers among the fringe tassels

sentences.zh: （明堂登歌設於堂上前楹間，宮架設於庭中）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall, ascent music is set between the front pillars of the hall above; the palace frame is set in the courtyard)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall, ascent music stands between the front hall pillars; the palace frame stands in the courtyard.)

sentences.zh: 前一日，設協律郎位二：一於壇上樂虡西北，一於宮架西北。

translations.literal: The day before, they set two Pitch-Pipe Officer positions: one northwest of the music stands on the altar platform, one northwest of the palace frame.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve, two pitch-pipe officers were posted—one northwest of the ascent-music stand on the altar, one northwest of the palace frame.

sentences.zh: 押樂官位二：太常丞於登歌樂虡北，太常卿於宮架北。

translations.literal: Two music-conductor officer positions: the Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices north of the ascent-music stands, the Director north of the palace frame.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising musicians stood north of the ascent stand and north of the palace frame—the vice director and director of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 省牲之夕，押樂太常卿及丞入行樂架，協律郎展視樂器。

translations.literal: On the evening of inspecting the sacrificial victim, the conducting Director and Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices entered the portable music frames; the Pitch-Pipe Officer spread and inspected the instruments.
translations.idiomatic: On the victim-inspection evening, the director and vice director entered the frame and the pitch-pipe officer examined every instrument.

sentences.zh: 祀之日，樂正帥工人、二舞以次入。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, the Chief Musician led workers and the two dances to enter in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day, the chief musician led the orchestra and both dances in, each in turn.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輿，自青城齋殿出，樂正撞景鍾，降輿入大次，景鍾止

translations.literal: The emperor rode the imperial carriage, coming out from the Qingcheng fasting hall; the Chief Musician struck the Splendor Bell; he descended the carriage and entered the great side-pavilion; the Splendor Bell stopped
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's carriage left the Qingcheng fasting hall, the chief musician struck the Splendor Bell; the emperor descended into the great pavilion and the bell fell silent

sentences.zh: （明堂不用景鍾）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall, the Splendor Bell is not used)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall does not use the Splendor Bell.)

sentences.zh: 服大裘袞冕，自正門入，協律郎跪，俯伏，舉麾，興。

translations.literal: Wearing the great fur robe and coronet robes, he entered from the main gate; the Pitch-Pipe Officer knelt, bowed prostrate, raised the baton, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: In great fur robe and full regalia he entered the main gate; the pitch-pipe officer knelt, bowed, raised his baton, and rose.

sentences.zh: 工鼓，宮架《乾安之樂》作，凡升降、行止皆奏之

translations.literal: The workers drummed; the palace frame performed the music "Peace to Qian"; for all ascending, descending, walking, and stopping it was played
translations.idiomatic: Musicians struck up; the palace frame played "Peace to Qian" for every ascent, descent, and step

sentences.zh: （明堂奏《儀安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Etiquette")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Rite.")

sentences.zh: 至午階版位，西向立，協律郎偃麾戛，樂止

translations.literal: Arriving at the south-side stair platform position, he stood facing west; the Pitch-Pipe Officer lowered the baton and stopped it; music ceased
translations.idiomatic: He reached the southern stair platform and stood facing west; the pitch-pipe officer lowered his baton and the music stopped

sentences.zh: （明堂至阼階下，樂止）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall, arriving below the east-side stairs, music stops)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall, music stops below the eastern stairs.)

sentences.zh: 凡樂，皆協律郎舉麾而後作，偃麾而後止。

translations.literal: For all music, only after the Pitch-Pipe Officer raises the baton does it begin; only after he lowers the baton does it stop.
translations.idiomatic: No music began until the pitch-pipe officer raised his baton, and none ceased until he lowered it.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請行事，宮架作《景安之樂》。

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner memorialized requesting to perform the rites; the palace frame performed the music "Peace to Splendor."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner requested commencement; the palace frame played "Peace to Splendor."

sentences.zh: （明堂作《誠安》。）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Sincerity.")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Sincerity.")

sentences.zh: 文舞進，左丞相等升，詣神位前，樂作，六成止。

translations.literal: The civil dance advanced; the Left Chancellor and others ascended, proceeded to before the spirit seat; music began and stopped at the sixth segment.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance advanced; the left chancellor and others ascended to the deity and music ran six movements, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 皇帝執大圭再拜，內侍進禦匜帨，宮架樂作，帨手畢，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor held the great scepter and bowed twice; inner attendants advanced the imperial ewer and towel; palace-frame music began; when towel-hands were finished, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice with the great scepter; attendants brought the imperial ewer and towel; palace music played until the cleansing was done, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使前導升壇，宮架樂作，至壇下，樂止。

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner led forward in ascending the altar; palace-frame music began; arriving below the altar, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him up the altar to music that ceased at the altar's foot.

sentences.zh: 升自午階，

translations.literal: He ascended from the south-side stairs,
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the south stair,

sentences.zh: （明堂並升自阼階。）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall, both ascend from the east-side stairs.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall, both ascend from the east stair.)

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，至壇上，樂止。

translations.literal: Ascent music began; arriving on the altar platform, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music played until he stood on the altar, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 登歌《嘉安之樂》作

translations.literal: Ascent music "Peace to Excellence" began
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music played "Peace to Excellence"

sentences.zh: （明堂至堂上作《鎮安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall, arriving in the hall above, they play "Peace to Suppression")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall, on entering the upper hall they play "Peace to Suppress.")

sentences.zh: 奠鎮圭、奠玉幣於上帝，樂止。

translations.literal: He set down the territorial scepter and presented jade disks and silk to High God; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the territorial scepter and jade and silk to High God, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 詣皇地祇、太祖、太宗神位前，如上儀。

translations.literal: He proceeded before the spirit seats of Imperial Earth Spirit, Taizu, and Taizong, following the same ritual as above.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated the rite at the seats of Earth, Taizu, and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使導還版位，登歌樂作，降階，樂止

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner led him back to the platform position; ascent music began; he descended the stairs; music stopped
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him back; ascent music played as he descended, then ceased

sentences.zh: （明堂降自阼階）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall, he descends from the east-side stairs)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall he descends the east stair.)

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，至版位，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace-frame music began; arriving at the platform position, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace-frame music played until he reached his station, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 奉俎官入正門，宮架《豐安之樂》作

translations.literal: The offering-tray officer entered the main gate; the palace frame performed "Peace to Abundance"
translations.idiomatic: The tray bearer entered the main gate to the palace frame's "Peace to Abundance"

sentences.zh: （明堂作《禧安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Fortune")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Fortune.")

sentences.zh: 跪，奠俎訖，樂止。

translations.literal: He knelt; when the offering tray was set down it was finished; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt, the offering was set, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 內侍以禦匜帨進，宮架樂作，帨手拭爵，樂止。

translations.literal: Inner attendants advanced the imperial ewer and towel; palace-frame music began; with towel in hand he wiped the goblet; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought the ewer and towel; music played while he wiped the cup, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使導升壇，宮架樂作，至午階，樂止。

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner led in ascending the altar; palace-frame music began; arriving at the south-side stairs, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him back up the altar; music ceased at the south stair.

sentences.zh: 升自午階，登歌樂作，至壇上，樂止

translations.literal: He ascended from the south-side stairs; ascent music began; arriving on the altar platform, music stopped
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the south stair to ascent music that ceased on the altar

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall there is no altar ascent)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall there is no altar ascent.)

translations.idiomatic: Ascent music played "Peace to Fortune"

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Celebration")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Celebration.")

sentences.zh: ，詣神位前，三祭酒，少立，樂止。

translations.literal: , he proceeded before the spirit seat, thrice offering libation, stood briefly; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ; he advanced to the deity, poured three libations, paused briefly, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 讀冊，皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: He read the document; the emperor bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The text was read; the emperor bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 每詣神位並如之。

translations.literal: Each time he proceeded to a spirit seat it was all as above.
translations.idiomatic: At every deity he followed the same order.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使導還版位，登歌樂作，降階，樂止。

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner led him back to the platform position; ascent music began; he descended the stairs; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him back; ascent music played as he descended, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，至版位，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace-frame music began; arriving at the platform position, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace-frame music played until he reached his station, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 奏請還小次，宮架樂作，入小次，樂止。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting return to the small side-pavilion; palace-frame music began; he entered the small side-pavilion; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was asked to return to the small pavilion; music played until he entered, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 武舞進，宮架《正安之樂》作

translations.literal: The martial dance advanced; the palace frame performed "Peace to Rectitude"
translations.idiomatic: The martial dance advanced; the palace frame played "Peace to Rectitude"

sentences.zh: （明堂作《穆安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Solemnity")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Solemnity.")

sentences.zh: 舞者立定，樂止。

translations.literal: The dancers stood fixed; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The dancers held their positions; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，升，詣酌尊所，西向立，宮架《正安之樂》作

translations.literal: The subordinate offering: he ascended, proceeded to the libation-vessel place, stood facing west; the palace frame performed "Peace to Rectitude"
translations.idiomatic: For the subordinate offering he ascended to the libation stand, faced west, and the palace frame played "Peace to Rectitude"

sentences.zh: （明堂皇太子為亞獻，作《穆安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall the heir apparent serves as subordinate offering; they play "Peace to Solemnity")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall the heir apparent is subordinate offering and they play "Peace to Solemnity.")

sentences.zh: 三祭酒，以次酌獻如上儀，樂止。

translations.literal: Thrice offering libation, in order performing libation offerings following the ritual above; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He poured three libations and offered wine at each seat in the same order; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 終獻亦如之。

translations.literal: The final offering was also as above.
translations.idiomatic: The final offering followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 奏請詣飲福位，宮架樂作，至午階，樂止。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to proceed to the drinking-fortune position; palace-frame music began; arriving at the south-side stairs, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was asked to advance to the fortune-drinking station; palace-frame music played until he reached the south stair, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 升自午階，登歌樂作，將至位，樂止。

translations.literal: He ascended from the south-side stairs; ascent music began; when he was about to reach the position, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the south stair to ascent music that ceased as he neared his station.

sentences.zh: 登歌《禧安之樂》作

translations.literal: Ascent music "Peace to Fortune" began
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music played "Peace to Fortune"

sentences.zh: （明堂作《胙安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Sacrificial Portion")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Sacrificial Portion.")

sentences.zh: 飲福，禮畢，樂止。

translations.literal: He drank fortune; the rite was complete; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He took the fortune cup; when the rite was finished, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使導還版位，登歌樂作，降階，樂止。

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner led him back to the platform position; ascent music began; he descended the stairs; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him back; ascent music played as he descended, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮架樂作，至版位，樂止

translations.literal: Palace-frame music began; arriving at the platform position, music stopped
translations.idiomatic: Palace-frame music played until he reached his station, then stopped

sentences.zh: （明堂不降階）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall he does not descend the stairs)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall he does not descend the stairs.)

sentences.zh: 徹豆，登歌《熙安之樂》作

translations.literal: The vessels were withdrawn; ascent music "Peace to Splendor" began
translations.idiomatic: As the offering vessels were cleared, ascent music played "Peace to Splendor"

sentences.zh: （明堂作《歆安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Delight")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Delight.")

sentences.zh: 送神，宮架《景安之樂》作，一成止

translations.literal: Escorting the spirits, the palace frame performed the music "Peace to Splendor"; one section and stop
translations.idiomatic: As the spirits were escorted out, the palace frame played "Peace to Splendor," one movement, then stopped

sentences.zh: （明堂作《誠安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Sincerity")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Sincerity.")

sentences.zh: 詣望燎、望瘞位，宮架樂作，至位，樂止

translations.literal: He proceeded to the overlook-burning and overlook-burying positions; palace-frame music began; arriving at the positions, music stopped
translations.idiomatic: He went to the pyre and burial outlooks to music that ceased on arrival

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall there is burning but no burial)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall there is burning but no burial.)

sentences.zh: 燎、瘞畢，還大次，宮架《乾安之樂》作

translations.literal: Burning and burial complete, returning to the great side-pavilion, the palace frame performed the music "Peace to Qian"
translations.idiomatic: When burning and burial were done, he returned to the great pavilion to the palace frame's "Peace to Qian"

sentences.zh: （明堂作《憩安》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Rest")〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall they play "Peace to Rest.")

sentences.zh: 至大次，樂止。

translations.literal: Arriving at the great side-pavilion, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Music ceased when he reached the great pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘大輦出大次，樂正撞景鍾

translations.literal: The emperor rode the great imperial carriage out from the great side-pavilion; the music director struck the Splendor Bell
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the great pavilion in the grand imperial carriage as the music director sounded the Splendor Bell

sentences.zh: （明堂不用景鍾）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall the Splendor Bell is not used)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall the Splendor Bell is not used.)

sentences.zh: ，鼓吹振作，降輦還齋殿，景鍾止。

translations.literal: , the wind ensemble was raised up; he descended the carriage and returned to the fasting hall; the Splendor Bell stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ; the wind and percussion ensemble struck up; he alighted and returned to the fasting hall, and the Splendor Bell fell silent.

sentences.zh: 百官、宗室班賀於端誠殿，奏請聖駕進發，軍樂導引，至麗正門，大樂正令奏《采茨之樂》，入門，樂止

translations.literal: The hundred officials and imperial clansmen filed to offer congratulations at the Duancheng Hall; he memorialized requesting the sacred carriage to set out; military music led; arriving at the Lizheng Gate, the Chief Director of Music ordered performed the music "Gathering Thistles"; entering the gate, music stopped
translations.idiomatic: Officials and clansmen offered congratulations at Duancheng Hall; the emperor was asked to depart; military music escorted him to Lizheng Gate, where the chief music director played "Gathering Thistles" until he entered and the music stopped

sentences.zh: （明堂就賀於紫宸殿，不奏《采茨》）〉

translations.literal: (For the Bright Hall congratulations are offered at the Zichen Hall, and "Gathering Thistles" is not performed)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall congratulations are held in Zichen Hall and "Gathering Thistles" is not played.)

sentences.zh: 乃禦麗正門肆赦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the Lizheng Gate to proclaim a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Lizheng Gate to proclaim a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 前期，太常設宮架樂於門之前，設鉦鼓於其西，皇帝升門至禦閣，大樂正令撞黃鍾之鍾，右五鍾皆應，《乾安之樂》作，升御坐，樂止。

translations.literal: In the preliminary period, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set palace-frame music before the gate, set gongs and drums to its west, the emperor ascended the gate to the imperial pavilion, the Chief Director of Music struck the Yellow Bell bell, the five bells to the right all resounded, the music "Peace to Qian" began, he ascended to the imperial seat, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set palace-frame music before the gate and gongs and drums west of it. The emperor climbed to the imperial pavilion; the chief music director struck the Yellow Bell and the five bells to the right answered; "Peace to Qian" played until he took the throne, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 金雞立，太常擊鼓，囚集，鼓聲止。

translations.literal: The golden rooster was set up; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices struck the drum; prisoners assembled; the drum sound stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The golden cock was raised; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices beat the drum until the prisoners were assembled, then silence.

sentences.zh: 宣製畢，大樂正令撞蕤賓之鍾，左五鍾皆應，皇帝還禦幄，樂止。

translations.literal: When the proclamation of the edict was finished, the Chief Director of Music struck the Flaming Guest bell, the five bells to the left all resounded, the emperor returned to the imperial canopy, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the amnesty text had been read, the chief director struck the Flaming Guest bell; the five bells to the left answered; the emperor withdrew to the canopy and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 乘輦降門，作樂，導引至文德殿，降輦，樂止。

translations.literal: Riding the carriage he descended the gate; music was performed; he was led to the Wende Hall; descended from the carriage; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He rode down from the gate to music that escorted him to Wende Hall; on alighting, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 按大禮用樂，凡三十有四色：歌色一，笛色二，塤色三，篪色四，笙色五，簫色六，編鍾七，編磬八，鎛鍾九，特磬十，琴十一，瑟十二，、十三，搏拊十四，晉鼓十五，建鼓十六，鞞、應鼓十七，雷鼓

translations.literal: According to the great ceremony's use of music, there are in all thirty-four timbre-colors: singing-color one, flute-color two, xun-color three, chi-color four, sheng-color five, xiao-color six, tuned-bell racks seven, tuned-chime racks eight, bo-bells nine, special chimes ten, zithers eleven, se twelve, zhu thirteen, hand-clappers fourteen, Jin drums fifteen, establishment drums sixteen, leather and response drums seventeen, thunder drums
translations.idiomatic: The great ceremonies employ thirty-four timbre-colors: voice, flute, xun, chi, sheng, xiao, tuned bell racks, tuned chime racks, bo-bells, special chimes, zithers, se, zhu, hand-clappers, Jin drums, establishment drums, leather and response drums, and thunder drums

translations.idiomatic: (Used in sacrifices to the Heavenly Spirit.)

translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth, thunder nao-drums

translations.idiomatic: (As above.)

translations.literal: Nineteen, spirit drums
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth, spirit drums

translations.idiomatic: (Used in sacrifices to earthly deities.)

translations.idiomatic: Twentieth, spirit nao-drums

translations.idiomatic: (As above.)

translations.idiomatic: (Used in ancestral temple feasts.)

translations.idiomatic: Twenty-second, dew nao-drums

translations.idiomatic: (As above.)

sentences.zh: 二十三，雅鼓二十四，相鼓二十五，單鞀鼓二十六，旌纛二十七，金鉦二十八，金錞二十九，單鐸三十，雙鐸三十一，鐃鐸三十二，奏坐三十三，麾幡三十四。

translations.literal: Twenty-three, ya-drums; twenty-four, xiang-drums; twenty-five, single nao-drums; twenty-six, banner standards; twenty-seven, golden gongs; twenty-eight, golden chimes; twenty-nine, single bo; thirty, paired bo; thirty-one, cymbal-bo; thirty-two, seated performance; thirty-three, command banners; thirty-four, command pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-third, ya-drums; twenty-fourth, xiang-drums; twenty-fifth, single nao-drums; twenty-sixth, banner standards; twenty-seventh, golden gongs; twenty-eighth, golden chimes; twenty-ninth, single bo; thirtieth, paired bo; thirty-first, cymbal-bo; thirty-second, seated performance; thirty-third, command banners; thirty-fourth, command pennants.

sentences.zh: 此國樂之用尤大者，故具載於篇。

translations.literal: These among the state's music uses are especially great; therefore they are fully recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: These instruments matter most in state music, and are therefore recorded here in full.

sentences.zh: 初，紹興崇建皇儲，詔有司備禮冊命，然在欽宗恤製，未及製樂。

translations.literal: At first, in Shaoxing they reverently established the imperial heir, and an edict ordered the relevant offices to prepare ritual, document, and investiture, yet they were in Emperor Qinzong's mourning compassion period and had not yet made music.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxing the court formally named an heir and ordered the bureaus to prepare the investiture rites, but Qinzong's mourning still held and no music could yet be composed.

sentences.zh: 乾道初元，詔立皇太子，命禮部、太常寺討論舊禮以聞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, an edict established the heir apparent and ordered the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to discuss former rites and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiandao an edict named the crown prince and charged the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to review past precedents and report.

sentences.zh: 受冊日，陳黃麾仗於大慶殿，設宮架樂於殿庭，皇帝升御坐，作《乾安之樂》，升，用黃鍾宮，降，用蕤賓宮。

translations.literal: On the day of receiving the document, the yellow banner guard array was displayed at the Daqing Hall, palace-frame music was set in the hall courtyard, the emperor ascended to the imperial seat, performed the music "Peace to Qian"; ascending used the Yellow Bell mode, descending used the Flaming Guest mode.
translations.idiomatic: On investiture day the yellow-banner guard was arrayed in Daqing Hall and palace-frame music set in the courtyard. As the emperor took the throne, "Peace to Qian" played—Yellow Bell mode for ascent, Flaming Guest for descent.

sentences.zh: 皇太子入殿門，作《明安之樂》，受冊出殿門亦如之，皆用應鍾宮。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent entered the hall gate, performed the music "Peace to Clarity"; receiving the document and leaving the hall gate were also the same, all using the Responding Bell mode.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince entered the hall gate, "Peace to Clarity" played; the same on receiving the patent and leaving—all in Responding Bell mode.

sentences.zh: 至七年，易應鍾而奏以姑洗。

translations.literal: By the seventh year, they changed from Responding Bell and played using Maiden Wash.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh year they switched from Responding Bell to Maiden Wash mode.

sentences.zh: 古者，太子生則太師吹管以度其聲，觀所協之律。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when the heir apparent was born the Grand Tutor blew the pipe to measure his voice and observe which pitch it harmonized with.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a prince was born the Grand Tutor sounded a pipe to measure his voice and see which pitch it matched.

sentences.zh: 有虞典樂教胄子，自天子之元子皆以樂為教，所以養其性情之正，蕩滌邪穢，消融查滓而和順於道德，則陳金石雅奏，以重元良。

translations.literal: In the era of Youyu, classical music taught the heir sons; from the primogenital son of the Son of Heaven all were taught with music—thereby nourishing the rectitude of their nature and disposition, washing away depravity and filth, melting away dregs and sediment and harmonizing with virtue and the Way; then they arrayed metal and stone with elegant performances to give weight to the primary heir.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity music trained the imperial sons: even the emperor's eldest was raised on it to straighten his nature, scour away vice, and settle his heart in virtue—then bronze and stone were set out in stately performance to honor the heir.

sentences.zh: 冊拜宜仿古誼，式昭盛禮。

translations.literal: The document-bowing ceremony should follow ancient principle to display fully the grand rite.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture should follow ancient precedent to display the full solemnity of the rite.

sentences.zh: 由唐季世，儲貳罕定，國家益多故而禮廢樂闕。

translations.literal: From the late Tang, the heir second was rarely fixed, the state ever more beset by troubles, and rites fell into ruin and music was wanting.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Tang onward heirs were rarely settled; troubles multiplied and ritual music fell away.

sentences.zh: 至於建隆定樂，雖詔皇太子出入奏《良安》，至道始冊皇太子，有司言：“太子受冊，宜奏《正安之樂》。

translations.literal: As for Jianlong's fixing of music, although an edict had the heir apparent enter and exit to the performance of "Good Peace," only in the Zhidao era was the heir apparent first enfeoffed with a document, when the relevant offices said: "When the heir apparent receives the document, it is appropriate to perform the music 'Peace to Rectitude.'"
translations.idiomatic: When music was fixed under Jianlong, heirs still entered and left to "Good Peace"; only in Zhidao was a crown prince first formally invested, and the bureaus said, "At investiture the crown prince should hear 'Peace to Rectitude.'"

sentences.zh: 百年曠典，至是舉行，中外胥悅。

translations.literal: A hundred-year neglected great precedent, at this time was carried out; within and without all rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: A century-old rite neglected was at last performed, to universal joy within and without.

sentences.zh: 至天禧冊命，禮儀院復奏改《正安之樂》。

translations.literal: At the investiture in Tianxi, the Institute of Ritual Protocol again memorialized changing to the music "Peace to Rectitude."
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianxi investiture the Institute of Ritual Protocol again petitioned to change the music to "Peace to Rectitude."

sentences.zh: 乾道之用《明安》，實祖述天禧，而以姑洗為宮，則唐東宮軒垂奏樂舊貫雲。

translations.literal: Qiandao's use of "Peace to Clarity" in truth followed Tianxi as ancestor, while taking Maiden Wash as tonal center—that was the old practice of music performed at the Tang Eastern Palace Xuanwei Hall, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao's "Peace to Clarity" truly followed Tianxi's precedent, while making Maiden Wash the tonal center—as was the old Tang practice of music at the Eastern Palace's Xuanwei Hall.

sentences.zh: 孝宗素恭儉，每賀正使赴宴作樂，多遇上辛齋禁，有司條治平用樂典故以進。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong was by nature respectful and frugal; whenever New Year's envoys came to banquets with music performed, he often encountered the Shangxin fasting prohibition; the relevant offices itemized the Zhiping-era precedents for using music and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was respectful and frugal by nature; whenever New Year envoys came to court banquets with music, the day often fell under Shangxin fasting rules, and the bureaus laid out Zhiping-era precedents on ritual music for his review.

sentences.zh: 及生辰使上壽，適親郊散齋，樞密副使陳俊卿請以禮諭北使，毋用樂。

translations.literal: When envoys for the birthday came to offer longevity congratulations, it happened to coincide with the dispersal fast before the suburban sacrifice; Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Chen Junqing asked to use ritual to instruct the northern envoys not to use music.
translations.idiomatic: When birthday envoys came to offer congratulations, the court was in pre-suburban fasting; Vice Military Commissioner Chen Junqing urged using ritual to tell the Jin envoys to forgo music.

sentences.zh: 不得已，則上壽之日設樂，而宣旨罷之，及宴使人，然後用之，庶存事天之誠。

translations.literal: If there was no alternative, then on the day of offering longevity music would be set up, yet an edict would be proclaimed to stop it; only when banqueting the envoys afterward was it then used—thus to preserve the sincerity of serving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If there was no choice, music would be arranged for the longevity rite but an edict would cancel it; only at the envoy's feast would it be used—to preserve sincerity toward Heaven.

sentences.zh: 上可其奏，且曰：“宴殿雖進禦酒，亦勿用。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this memorial, and said: "Even though the banquet hall presents imperial wine, still do not use it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and said, "Even when the banquet hall serves imperial wine, do not use music."

sentences.zh: ”宰相葉顒、魏杞方主用樂之議，以為樂奏於紫宸，乃使客之禮。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers Ye Yong and Wei Qi were then advocating the use of music, holding that music played at the Zichen Hall was ritual toward envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Ye Yong and Wei Qi were then arguing for music, maintaining that performance in Zichen Hall was proper etiquette toward envoys.

sentences.zh: 俊卿獨奏曰：“適奉詔旨，仰見聖學高明，過古帝王遠甚。

translations.literal: Junqing alone memorialized, saying: "Just now receiving the imperial edict, I look up and see Your Sage-learning lofty and bright, surpassing ancient emperors and kings by far.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing alone memorialized: "Having just received Your edict, I see Your sage-learning surpasses the ancient emperors and kings by far.

sentences.zh: 彼初未嚐必欲用樂，而我乃望風希意，自為失禮以徇之，他日輕侮，何所不至？

translations.literal: They at first had not necessarily insisted on using music, yet we would look to the wind and guess their intent, ourselves losing ritual to indulge them—another day, what contempt would not reach any limit?"
translations.idiomatic: They had not initially insisted on music, yet we would guess their wishes and break ritual to please them—what insult would not follow?"

sentences.zh: ”尋詔：“垂拱上壽止樂，正殿猶為北使權用。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward an edict: "At the Shuigong Hall, longevity rites stop music; at the main hall it may still be used provisionally for the northern envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ran: "Stop music for longevity rites in Shuigong; the main hall may still provisionally use it for the Jin envoys."

sentences.zh: ”後三年，賀使當朝辭，復值散齋，上乃諭館伴以決意去樂及議所以處之者，如使人必以作樂為言，則移茶酒就驛管領，遂有更不用樂之詔。

translations.literal: " Three years later, when the congratulatory envoys were to take leave at court, they again encountered dispersal fasting; the emperor then instructed the reception officers of his firm resolve to remove music and to discuss how to handle it—if the envoys certainly insisted on music, then tea and wine would be moved to the relay station for hosting—and thereupon came a further edict not to use music at all.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, when envoys came to take leave, fasting coincided again; the emperor told the reception officers of his resolve to drop music and how to handle it—if envoys insisted, tea and wine would be served at the relay station—and a new edict abolished music altogether.

sentences.zh: 其後因雨澤愆期，分禱天地、宗廟，精修雩祀。

translations.literal: Afterward, because rain and moisture were overdue, they divided prayers to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple and carefully performed the rain-sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when rains were overdue, the court prayed separately to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples and carefully conducted the rain rite.

sentences.zh: 按禮，大雩，帝用盛樂。

translations.literal: According to the rites, for the great rain-prayer the emperor uses full music.
translations.idiomatic: The rites prescribed full music for the great rain prayer.

sentences.zh: 而唐開元祈雨雩壇，謂之特祀，乃不以樂薦。

translations.literal: Yet in Tang Kaiyuan's rain-prayer altar they called it a special sacrifice and did not present it with music.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under Tang Kaiyuan the rain altar was treated as a special sacrifice and offered without music.

sentences.zh: 於是太常朱時敏言：“《通典》載雩禮用舞僮歌《雲漢》，晉蔡謨議謂：‘《雲漢》之詩，興於宣王，歌之者取其修德禳災，以和陰陽之義。

translations.literal: Thereupon Director of Imperial Sacrifices Zhu Shimin said: "The Comprehensive Institutions records that the rain rite uses dancing youths to sing 'Vast Galaxy'; Jin Grand Mentor Cai Mo's discussion said: 'The ode "Vast Galaxy" arose under King Xuan; those who sang it took its meaning of cultivating virtue to avert disaster and harmonize yin and yang.'"
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhu Shimin of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "The Comprehensive Institutions records rain rites performed by dancing boys singing 'Vast Galaxy.' Cai Mo of Jin argued that the poem arose under King Xuan and that singers drew on its theme of cultivating virtue to ward off disaster and harmonize yin and yang."

sentences.zh: ’乞用舞僮六十四人，衣玄衣，歌《雲漢》之詩。

translations.literal: ' I beg to use sixty-four dancing youths, dressed in dark robes, to sing the ode "Vast Galaxy."
translations.idiomatic: He requested sixty-four dancing boys in black robes to sing the "Vast Galaxy" ode.

sentences.zh: ”詔亟從之。

translations.literal: " An edict immediately followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it at once.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，詔以上皇加上尊號，立春日行慶壽禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, an edict had the retired emperor given an honorific title, and on the Establishment of Spring day they conducted the longevity-celebration rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 an edict added honorific titles for the retired emperor and scheduled a longevity celebration for Establishment of Spring.

sentences.zh: 有司尋言：“乾道加尊號，用宮架三十六，樂工共一百一十三人。

translations.literal: The relevant offices soon said: "When honorific titles were added in Qiandao, thirty-six palace-frame racks were used, musicians totaling one hundred thirteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus soon reported: "At the Qiandao honorific ceremony thirty-six palace-frame racks were used with 113 musicians.

sentences.zh: 今來加號慶壽，事體尤重，合依大禮例，用四十八架，樂正、樂工用一百八十八人，庶得禮樂明備。

translations.literal: Now for adding titles and celebrating longevity, the affair in body is especially weighty; it should follow the great ceremony precedent, using forty-eight racks, music directors and musicians using one hundred eighty-eight persons—thus to obtain ritual and music clear and complete."
translations.idiomatic: This celebration is weightier still; by great-rite precedent forty-eight racks and 188 directors and musicians are needed so ritual and music may be fully equipped."

sentences.zh: ”仍令分就太常寺、貢院前五日教習。

translations.literal: " They were still ordered to divide and rehearse at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and before the examination compound five days prior.
translations.idiomatic: They were to rehearse separately at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the examination yard five days beforehand.

sentences.zh: 前期，太常設宮架之樂於大慶殿，協律郎位於宮架西北，東向；

translations.literal: In the preliminary period, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set palace-frame music at the Daqing Hall; the pitch-pipe officer's position was northwest of the palace frame, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the Court set palace-frame music in Daqing Hall; the pitch-pipe officer stood northwest of the frame, facing east;

sentences.zh: 押樂太常卿位於宮架之北，北向；

translations.literal: the Director of Imperial Sacrifices supervising music stood north of the palace frame, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: the supervising director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stood north of the frame, facing north;

sentences.zh: 皇太子及文武百僚，並位於宮架之北，東西相向，又設宮架於德壽殿門外，協律郎、太常卿位如之。

translations.literal: the heir apparent and civil and military hundred officials were all positioned north of the palace frame, facing each other east and west; palace-frame music was also set outside the gate of the Deshou Palace, pitch-pipe officer and Director of Imperial Sacrifices positions as above.
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince and civil and military officials stood north of the frame facing one another east and west; a second frame was set outside Deshou Palace gate with the same placements.

sentences.zh: 及發冊寶日，儀仗、鼓吹列於大慶殿門，樂正、師二人以次入。

translations.literal: On the day of issuing documents and treasures, ceremonial guards and wind ensemble were arrayed at the Daqing Hall gate; music directors and masters, two persons, entered in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the patent and seals were issued, guards and wind music lined the Daqing Hall gate; two music directors entered in turn.

sentences.zh: 讚者引押樂太常卿、協律郎入，就位，奏中嚴外辦訖，禮儀使奏請皇帝恭行發冊寶之禮，太常卿導冊寶，《正安之樂》作。

translations.literal: The announcer led in the Director of Imperial Sacrifices supervising music and the pitch-pipe officer; they took position; performed that inner solemnity and outer readiness were complete; the Ritual Protocol Commissioner memorialized requesting the emperor respectfully to perform the rite of issuing documents and treasures; the Director of Imperial Sacrifices guided the documents and treasures; the music "Peace to Rectitude" began.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer led in the supervising director and pitch-pipe officer to their stations; inner and outer readiness was reported complete; the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to perform the issuance rite; the director of sacrifices guided in the patent and seals to "Peace to Rectitude."

sentences.zh: 中書令奉寶、侍中奉冊進行，《禮安之樂》作。

translations.literal: The Chief Counselor of the Secretariat bore the seal, the Palace Attendant bore the patent in procession, and the music "Ritual Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief counselor bore the seal and the palace attendant the patent in procession while "Ritual Peace" was played.

sentences.zh: 發寶冊畢，鼓吹振作，儀衛等以次從行。

translations.literal: When issuing the seal and patent was finished, wind and percussion ensembles sounded forth; ceremonial guards and the like followed in order.
translations.idiomatic: Once the seal and patent had been issued, wind ensembles struck up and the guard retinue followed in order.

sentences.zh: 皇帝自祥曦殿輦至德壽宮行禮，冊寶入殿門，作《正安之樂》。

translations.literal: The emperor by carriage from the Xiangxi Hall proceeded to the Virtue-and-Longevity Palace to perform the rites; when the patent and seal entered the hall gate, the music "Correct Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode from Xiangxi Hall to the Virtue-and-Longevity Palace; when the patent and seal passed the hall gate, "Correct Peace" sounded.

sentences.zh: 上皇出宮，作《乾安之樂》；

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor came out of the palace, the music "Qian Peace" was performed;
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor left the palace, "Qian Peace" was played;

sentences.zh: 升御坐，奉上冊寶，作《聖安之樂》；

translations.literal: ascending to the imperial seat, presenting the patent and seal above, the music "Sagely Peace" was performed;
translations.idiomatic: as he took the throne and presented the patent and seal, "Sagely Peace" was played;

sentences.zh: 降御坐，作《乾安》之樂。

translations.literal: descending from the imperial seat, the music "Qian Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: and when he stepped down, "Qian Peace" sounded again.

sentences.zh: 太后冊寶進行，用《正安》；

translations.literal: For the Empress Dowager's patent and seal in procession, "Correct Peace" was used;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's patent and seal procession used "Correct Peace";

sentences.zh: 出閣升坐，用《坤安》；

translations.literal: coming out of the side chamber and ascending to sit, "Earthly Peace" was used;
translations.idiomatic: leaving the side chamber to take her seat, "Earthly Peace";

sentences.zh: 降坐入閣，復作《坤安之樂》。

translations.literal: descending from the seat and entering the side chamber, "Earthly Peace" was again performed.
translations.idiomatic: and returning to the side chamber, "Earthly Peace" again.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書趙雄等言：“國朝舊制，車駕出，奏樂。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zhao Xiong and others said: "By our dynasty's old system, when the imperial carriage goes out, music is performed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Zhao Xiong and others argued: "Dynastic precedent requires music whenever the imperial carriage goes abroad.

sentences.zh: 今慶典之行，亙古未有，自非禮儀祥備，無以副中外歡愉之心。

translations.literal: Now this celebration in procession is without precedent since antiquity; unless ritual and ceremony are auspiciously complete, there is no way to answer the joyful hearts inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: This celebration is unprecedented; unless the rites are fully splendid, they cannot satisfy the joy of court and realm.

sentences.zh: 請慶壽行禮日，聖駕往還並用樂及簪花。

translations.literal: We beg that on the day of performing the longevity-celebration rites, the sacred carriage going and returning alike use music and flower pins.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that on the longevity rite the emperor's going and returning both use music and floral pins."

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而太常又言：“郊禋禮成，宜進胙慈闈，行上壽飲酒禮。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Court of Imperial Sacrifices again said: "When the suburban sacrifice rite is complete, it is appropriate to present sacrificial meat to the Cining quarters and perform the longevity toast and drinking rite.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Sacrifices added: "After the suburban sacrifice, sacrificial meat should be brought to Cining and the longevity toast performed.

sentences.zh: 所有上壽合辦仙樓仍用樂，某樂人照天申節禮例。

translations.literal: All arrangements for the longevity toast at the Immortal Tower should still use music; certain musicians following the Tian Shen festival ritual precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Immortal Tower arrangements should still include music, with musicians following the Tian Shen festival precedent."

sentences.zh: ”凡上詣德壽宮，或恭請上皇遊幸，或至南內，或上皇命同宴遊，或時序賞適、過宮侍宴，或聖節張樂、珥花、奉玉卮為上皇壽，率從容竟日，隆重養至樂，備極情文。

translations.literal: " Whenever the emperor went to the Virtue-and-Longevity Palace, or respectfully invited the Retired Emperor on tours, or went to the Southern Inner Palace, or the Retired Emperor ordered shared feasts and outings, or at seasonal pleasures passed the palace to attend banquets, or on sacred festivals spread music, wore flower pins, and presented jade goblets to wish the Retired Emperor longevity—in every case he was at ease through the day, honoring nurture to the utmost in music, with feeling and pattern fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: Whether visiting the Virtue-and-Longevity Palace, inviting the retired emperor on tours, entering the Southern Inner Palace, sharing banquets at his command, passing the palace for seasonal feasts, or on sacred festivals spreading music, wearing flowers, and offering jade cups for his longevity—the emperor was unhurried all day, honoring him with music and every courtesy of feeling and form.

sentences.zh: 及高宗之喪，孝宗力行三年之製，有司雖未嚐別設樂禁，而過期不忍聞樂。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, Xiaozong vigorously practiced the three-year regulation; although the relevant offices had not specially set a music prohibition, after the period expired he still could not bear to hear music.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's death Xiaozong observed three years of mourning; though no formal music ban was issued, he could not bear music even after the mourning term.

sentences.zh: 金使以會慶節來賀，稽之舊典，引對使人或許上壽，惟輟樂不舉。

translations.literal: Jin envoys came to congratulate on the Assembly Celebration festival; checking old canons, when leading envoys in audience one might permit the longevity toast, only suspending music and not performing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys came for the Assembly Celebration, precedent allowed the longevity toast in audience but not music.

sentences.zh: 孝宗斷以禮典，卻其書幣，就館遣行。

translations.literal: Xiaozong decided by ritual canon, declined their letters and gifts, and sent them off from the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong ruled by ritual canon, refused their letters and gifts, and dismissed them from the lodge.

sentences.zh: 次年再至，始用紹興故事，移宴於館而不作樂。

translations.literal: The next year when they came again, they first used the Shaoxing precedent, moving the feast to the lodge and not performing music.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court followed Shaoxing precedent: the feast moved to the lodge without music.

sentences.zh: 高宗升祔，太常言：“祔饗行禮，當設登歌、宮架、樂舞，晨祼饋食，其用樂如朝饗之製。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was elevated to collective enshrinement, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "For the enshrinement feast and performance of rites, ascent music, palace frame, and dances should be set up; for the morning libation and food offering, music should be used as in the morning feast regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was collectively enshrined, Imperial Sacrifices urged ascent music, palace frame, and dance for the enshrinement feast, with morning libation music as at the morning feast.

sentences.zh: ”於是，高宗廟昉奏《大德之樂》舞。

translations.literal: " Thereupon at Gaozong's temple they first performed the music-dance "Great Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozong's temple then first performed the "Great Virtue" dance.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：“今虞祔之行，純用古禮，導引神主，自有衛仗及太常鼓吹，而雜用道、釋，於禮非經，乞行蠲免。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Now for Yu's enshrinement procession, pure ancient rites are used; leading the spirit tablet already has guard arrays and Imperial Sacrifices wind ensembles—yet mixing in Daoist and Buddhist elements is not canonical in ritual; we beg that these be exempted and removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites argued: "Yu Di's enshrinement follows pure ancient rite—escorting the tablet already has guards and Imperial Sacrifices wind music—so Daoist and Buddhist additions are uncanonical; please remove them."

sentences.zh: ”詔從其請。

translations.literal: " An edict followed the request.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 即而大享明堂，起居舍人鄭僑奏：“祭祀於事為大，禮樂於用為急，然先王處此，有常變之不同，各務當其禮而已。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, at the great feast at the Bright Hall, Attendant Gentleman Zheng Qiao memorialized: "Sacrifice in affairs is great; ritual and music in use is urgent—yet former kings handling this had differences between constant practice and change, each striving only to suit its rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the great Bright Hall feast, Attendant Gentleman Zheng Qiao argued: "Sacrifice is supreme among affairs and ritual music urgent—yet former kings balanced constant practice and change, each suiting the rite at hand.

sentences.zh: 昔舜居堯喪，三載遏密，後世既用漢文以日易月之文，又用漢儒越紼行事之製，循習既久，不特用禮而又用樂，去古愈遠。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun dwelt in Yao's mourning, three years of suppressed sound; later ages both used Emperor Wen of Han's text of replacing days for months, and also used Han scholars' practice of stepping over the mourning hem to perform affairs—long followed in habit, not only using rites but also using music, growing farther from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Shun mourned Yao three years in silence; later ages adopted Han Wendi's day-for-month mourning and Han scholars' stepping the mourning hem—habit so long entrenched that rites and music both persisted, ever farther from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 聖主躬服通喪，有司請舉大禮，屈意從之。

translations.literal: The sage ruler personally wore full mourning; the relevant offices requested holding the great ceremony, and he bent his intent to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: The sage ruler wore full mourning himself; when offices urged the great ceremony, he yielded.

sentences.zh: 且大饗之禮，祭天地也，聖主身親行之，行禮作樂，似不可廢。

translations.literal: Moreover the great feast rite sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; the sage ruler performs it in person—performing rites and making music seemingly cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The great feast sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the ruler performs it in person—rite and music there seem indispensable.

sentences.zh: 其他官分獻與夫先期奏告例用樂者，權宜蠲寢，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: For other officials' divided offerings and for advance memorial announcements that by precedent use music—might it not also be acceptable provisionally to suspend and omit them?
translations.idiomatic: Could officials' separate offerings and advance announcements that use music by precedent be suspended instead?

sentences.zh: 今若因明堂損益而裁定之，亦足為將來法。

translations.literal: Now if through Bright Hall reductions and additions we decide and fix this, it would also suffice as law for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Settling this through Bright Hall adjustments would serve as law for the future.

sentences.zh: ”乃命太常討論，始詔除降神、奠玉幣、奉俎、酌獻、換舞、徹豆、送神依曲禮作樂外，所有皇帝及獻官盥洗、登降等樂皆備而不作雲。

translations.literal: " They then ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to discuss it; an edict first removed all except: sending down the spirit, offering jade and silks, presenting the meat stand, pouring libations, changing dances, removing beans, and sending off the spirit—according to the Rites of Zhou performing music—while all music for the emperor and offering officials at washing, ascending, and descending was prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: " Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to deliberate; the court decreed music only for sending down the spirit, offering jade and silks, presenting the stand, libations, dance changes, removing beans, and sending off the spirit per the Rites of Zhou—while music for the emperor's and officials' washing and ascent was set out but silenced.
